papers.title: Uptake of hepatitis B vaccination among nursing students in Cameroon: a mixed-methods study.
papers.abstract: SETTING: Three purposively identified nursing education institutions (Ayos, EITMS/GS, and the Virginia Henderson Foundation) in the Centre Region of Cameroon. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the psychological, socio-cognitive, economic, and institutional factors associated with hepatitis B (HBV) vaccine uptake among nursing students. DESIGN: A mixed-methods cross-sectional study was conducted between June and July 2025. Quantitative data (n = 325) were collected via self-administered electronic surveys, supplemented by qualitative focus group discussions. Quantitative analysis was performed using SPSS. Qualitative themes were synthesised via a hybrid inductive-deductive thematic analysis, using QCAmap. RESULTS: HBV vaccination was critically low at 29.54%, with only 50.04% of those vaccinated completing the full three-dose series. Multivariate analysis identified female gender, age, advanced study level, a solid knowledge level, high perceived self-efficacy, low vaccine-related anxiety, and encouragement from the educational institution as significant predictors of uptake. Qualitative findings highlighted as primary barriers: prohibitive costs, inadequate information, weak institutional mandates, and traditional prejudices. CONCLUSION: Immunisation rates among high-risk nursing students are alarmingly insufficient. To mitigate occupational risk, public health policy should mandate HBV vaccination at school matriculation and implement subsidies to facilitate economic access together with systematic sensitisation.

analysis.summary_en: This mixed-methods study investigated the factors influencing hepatitis B vaccine uptake among nursing students in Cameroon. It found that vaccination rates were critically low, with only 29.54% of students receiving the vaccine and 50.04% completing the full series. Multivariate analysis identified gender, age, study level, knowledge, self-efficacy, anxiety, and institutional encouragement as significant predictors of uptake. Qualitative findings highlighted cost, information gaps, weak mandates, and traditional prejudices as key barriers. The authors concluded that immunisation rates are insufficient and recommended policy interventions such as vaccination mandates and subsidies. The study's cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data limit its evidence strength, which is assessed as moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估护生中与乙型肝炎 (HBV) 疫苗 摄取相关的心理、社会认知、经济和制度因素。这项研究的动机是需要解决高风险医护人员免疫接种率不足的问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2025 年 6 月至 7 月期间,在喀麦隆中部地区的三个有意确定的护理教育机构(Ayos、EITMS/GS 和弗吉尼亚亨德森基金会)进行了一项混合方法横断面研究。通过自我管理的电子调查收集定量数据(n = 325),并辅以定性焦点小组讨论。
elements_zh.methods: 使用SPSS进行定量分析。使用 QCAmap 通过混合归纳演绎主题分析来合成定性主题。
elements_zh.main_results: HBV 疫苗接种 的比例极低,为 29.54%,只有 50.04% 的疫苗接种者完成了完整的三剂系列。多变量分析确定女性性别、年龄、高级学习水平、扎实的知识水平、高自我效能感、低 疫苗 相关焦虑以及来自教育机构的鼓励是吸收的重要预测因素。定性研究结果强调了主要障碍:高昂的成本、信息不足、机构授权薄弱和传统偏见。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为高危护生中免疫接种率严重不足的证据,强调需要采取有针对性的干预措施来提高 疫苗 的吸收率。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为公共卫生政策提供信息,建议在学校入学时实施 HBV 疫苗接种 指令,并提供补贴以促进经济准入,同时进行系统宣传。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横断面设计的限制,它没有建立因果关系,而且调查中可能存在自我报告偏差。由于依赖自我报告的数据并且关注单一地理区域,证据的强度中等。

papers.title: A New Nomogram for Mortality Prediction Within 5 Years in Portal Vein Thrombosis due to Hepatitis B-Related Cirrhosis.
papers.abstract: This study aims to develop a nomogram model intended for predicting long-term mortality in patients suffering from hepatitis B-related cirrhosis associated with Portal vein thrombosis (PVT). A total of 961 patients were recruited from January 2015 to December 2023, forming the training cohort. We analysed independent risk factors affecting 5-year mortality through COX regression, from which we constructed a nomogram. To assess the nomogram's utility, we employed the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, C-index, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The independent prognostic factors retained in the final model for patients with hepatitis B-related cirrhosis complicated by PVT included age (HR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.06-1.11; p < 0.001), leukocyte count (WBC) (HR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.03-1.17; p = 0.002), and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) (HR = 1.29, 95% CI: 1.22-1.35; p < 0.001), along with serum sodium (HR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.90-0.98; p = 0.005). The AUROC values for the nomogram were 0.906 (95% CI: 0.891-0.921) in the training cohort and 0.910 (95% CI: 0.885-0.927) in the validation cohort, demonstrating improved performance and discriminatory ability compared to current models, including CTP and MELD scores. Age, leukocyte count (WBC), NLR, and serum sodium emerged as independent risk factors impacting prognosis for patients with hepatitis B cirrhosis and PVT within 5 years. The nomogram developed in this research holds significant potential for accurately predicting the outcomes of these patients within 5 years.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the unmet need for accurate long-term mortality prediction in patients with hepatitis B-related cirrhosis complicated by portal vein thrombosis (PVT), a high-risk subgroup with limited prognostic tools.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort of 961 patients with hepatitis B-related cirrhosis and PVT was recruited from January 2015 to December 2023 and formed the training cohort for model development.
analysis.methods: Independent risk factors for 5-year mortality were identified using Cox regression, and a nomogram was constructed from these factors; model performance was assessed with ROC curves, C-index, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.
analysis.main_results: The nomogram achieved AUROC values of 0.906 (95% CI: 0.891–0.921) in the training cohort and 0.910 (95% CI: 0.885–0.927) in the validation cohort, outperforming Child–Turcotte–Pugh and MELD scores.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the nomogram as a significant advance in individualized risk stratification for this patient group, highlighting its improved discrimination compared to existing scoring systems.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The nomogram could inform clinical decision-making by enabling earlier identification of high-risk patients for intensified monitoring or therapeutic interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-centre, retrospective design and lack of external validation limit generalisability; the evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to potential selection and confounding biases.

Independent prognostic factors included age, leukocyte count, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and serum sodium. The model demonstrated high discriminatory performance with AUROC values of 0.906 in training and 0.910 in validation, outperforming Child–Turcotte–Pugh and MELD scores. The authors propose the nomogram as a clinically useful tool for individualized risk stratification in this high-risk subgroup.

papers.title: Validation of a Point-Of-Care Ultrasound for Hepatitis Among Front-Line Healthcare Workers Managing Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection in Zambia.
papers.abstract: To close gaps in implementing care of people with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in resource-limited settings, we evaluated the accuracy of a novel liver point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) protocol for hepatitis (PUSH) among front-line non-radiology healthcare workers in Zambia. At University Teaching Hospital in Lusaka, Zambia, from March to June 2024, we trained four nurses and six physicians with experience in HBV management, but not in ultrasound (US), in the PUSH protocol, which includes visualizing the liver in three windows (epigastric, subcostal and right transcostal) to identify cirrhosis-suggestive features and liver lesions suspicious for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Then, consecutive adult participants with chronic hepatitis B (PWHB) alone or HBV/HIV coinfection underwent PUSH with operators blinded to clinical data. We evaluated the accuracy of PUSH for significant fibrosis and cirrhosis using transient elastography (TE) as the reference standard test (RST) and for liver lesions that were possible HCC using a comprehensive abdominal ultrasound by an experienced radiographer as the RST. Nonparametric analysis of the receiver operating curve (ROC) for PUSH was adjusted for operator type (doctor vs. nurse), sex and HIV status. Among 197 PWHBs analysed, 69.5% were taking HBV antivirals and 27.9% had HBV/HIV. According to RSTs, 17.7% of PWHBs had significant fibrosis, 11.6% had cirrhosis and 3.5% had liver lesions. PUSH had low accuracy for significant fibrosis, with sensitivity of 8.3% (17.5-41.4), specificity of 100.0% (96.1-100) and an area under the curve (AUROC) of 0.54 (0.43-0.65), moderate accuracy for cirrhosis, with sensitivity of 60.9% (38.5-80.3), specificity of 97.7% (94.2-99.4) and AUROC of 0.79 (0.69-0.89), and higher accuracy for liver lesions, with 85.7% (42.1-99.6) sensitivity, 98.4% (95.5-99.7) specificity, AUROC of 0.92 (0.78-1.00). After an expedited training, front-line nurses and physicians treating HBV in Zambia were able to use PUSH to diagnose cirrhosis with moderate accuracy and liver lesions with high accuracy, although confidence intervals around performance estimates were wide. Liver POCUS including PUSH may be useful in HBV management when laboratory systems and TE are lacking.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the need to improve hepatitis B virus (HBV) care in resource-limited settings by evaluating a novel point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) protocol (PUSH) for diagnosing HBV-related liver disease among front-line healthcare workers in Zambia.
analysis.study_design_and_population: At University Teaching Hospital in Lusaka, Zambia, from March to June 2024, four nurses and six physicians with HBV management experience but no ultrasound training were trained in the PUSH protocol, which assesses liver cirrhosis-suggestive features and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) lesions in three windows.
analysis.methods: Consecutive adult participants with chronic hepatitis B (PWHB) alone or HBV/HIV coinfection underwent PUSH with operators blinded to clinical data, and accuracy was evaluated using transient elastography (TE) as the reference standard for fibrosis and cirrhosis and comprehensive abdominal ultrasound by an experienced radiographer for liver lesions.
analysis.main_results: Among 197 PWHBs, 17.7% had significant fibrosis, 11.6% had cirrhosis, and 3.5% had liver lesions; PUSH showed low accuracy for significant fibrosis (sensitivity 8.3%, specificity 100.0%, AUROC 0.54), moderate accuracy for cirrhosis (sensitivity 60.9%, specificity 97.7%, AUROC 0.79), and high accuracy for liver lesions (sensitivity 85.7%, specificity 98.4%, AUROC 0.92).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that PUSH can diagnose cirrhosis with moderate accuracy and liver lesions with high accuracy after expedited training, highlighting its potential utility in HBV management where laboratory systems and TE are lacking.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that PUSH could support HBV care in resource-limited settings by enabling front-line healthcare workers to identify cirrhosis and HCC lesions, potentially improving early diagnosis and referral pathways.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s limitations include wide confidence intervals around performance estimates and reliance on a single-center, short-duration training, which may limit generalisability and precision of accuracy metrics.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated a point-of-care ultrasound protocol (PUSH) for diagnosing hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver disease among front-line healthcare workers in Zambia. After brief training, nurses and physicians used PUSH to assess liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) lesions in adults with chronic HBV or HBV/HIV coinfection. Using transient elastography and expert ultrasound as reference standards, PUSH showed low accuracy for significant fibrosis (AUROC 0.54), moderate accuracy for cirrhosis (AUROC 0.79), and high accuracy for liver lesions (AUROC 0.92). The authors conclude that PUSH may be useful for HBV management in settings lacking laboratory infrastructure, though confidence intervals were wide and the single-center design limits generalisability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究通过评估用于诊断赞比亚一线医护人员中 HBV 相关肝病的新型护理点超声 (POCUS) 方案 (PUSH),解决了在资源有限的环境中改善 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 护理的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 3 月至 6 月,在赞比亚卢萨卡的大学教学医院,四名护士和六名具有乙肝管理经验但没有接受过超声培训的医生接受了 PUSH 方案培训,该方案在三个窗口中评估肝硬化提示特征和肝细胞癌 (HCC) 病变。
elements_zh.methods: 单独感染 慢性乙型肝炎 (PWHB) 或 HBV/HIV 合并感染的连续成人参与者在不了解临床数据的操作员的情况下接受 PUSH,并使用瞬时弹性成像 (TE) 作为纤维化和肝硬化的参考标准以及由经验丰富的肝脏病变放射技师进行综合腹部超声评估准确性。
elements_zh.main_results: 197名感染者中,17.7%有明显纤维化,11.6%有肝硬化,3.5%有肝脏病变;PUSH 对显着纤维化的准确性较低(敏感性 8.3%,特异性 100.0%,AUROC 0.54),对肝硬化的准确性中等(敏感性 60.9%,特异性 97.7%,AUROC 0.79),对肝脏病变的准确性较高(敏感性 85.7%,特异性 98.4%,AUROC 0.92)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,经过快速培训后,PUSH 可以以中等准确度诊断肝硬化,并以较高准确度诊断肝脏病变,这突显了其在缺乏实验室系统和 TE 的 HBV 管理中的潜在用途。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,PUSH 可以通过使一线医护人员识别肝硬化和 HCC 病变来支持资源有限环境中的 HBV 护理,从而有可能改善早期 诊断 和转诊途径。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括表现估计的置信区间较宽,以及对单中心、短期训练的依赖,这可能会限制准确性指标的普遍性和精度。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究通过评估用于诊断赞比亚一线医护人员中 HBV 相关肝病的新型护理点超声 (POCUS) 方案 (PUSH),解决了在资源有限的环境中改善 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 护理的需要。

papers.title: High screening coverage and positivity rates of HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B among pregnant women accessing antenatal care in Sierra Leone.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sierra Leone faces high rates of mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of HIV, syphilis, and presumed hepatitis B (HepB). Since 2014, integrated testing and treatment within antenatal care (ANC) have aimed to prevent this transmission, yet no comprehensive study on these infections among pregnant women exists. OBJECTIVES: Assess screening coverage and test positivity for these infections in 21 health facilities in 4 districts, each representing Sierra Leone's four regions, to ensure national representation of triple elimination testing: Primary (12), Secondary (5), and Tertiary (4). METHOD: A cross-sectional analysis of secondary data from health-facility registers in Western Area Urban, Bombali, Bo, and Kenema districts, between November 2024 and October 2025, summarised as frequencies and proportions. RESULTS: Among 10,003 women attending their first ANC visit, screening coverage was 99.6% for HIV, 99.6% for syphilis, 92.9% for HepB, and 92.4% for all three infections. Test positivity was 4.9% for HIV, 1.3% for syphilis, and 4.0% for HepB. CONCLUSION: Triple-disease testing at ANC facilities in Sierra Leone is feasible and can achieve high coverage. The test-positivity rate for HepB suggests a considerable burden of maternal infection and ongoing MTCT. Still, there are currently no interventions to address this gap. Testing should be scaled-up urgently and followed by a programme for maternal treatment, safe delivery, and immunisation.

papers.title: GAMBARAN HASIL PEMERIKSAAN HEPATITIS B SURFACE ANTIGEN DAN ANTIBODI HEPATITIS C VIRUS PADA IBU HAMIL
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C remain public health problems that may cause serious complications in pregnant women and fetuses and can also be transmitted vertically from mother to baby. Early detection through laboratory examination during pregnancy is essential as an effort to prevent transmission and provide optimal management. This study aimed to determine the results of Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg) and Hepatitis C Virus Antibody (Anti-HCV) examinations among pregnant women at Manding Public Health Center, Sumenep Regency. The study sample consisted of 32 pregnant women in the first and second trimesters who underwent laboratory examinations at Manding Public Health Center. The samples were selected using a purposive sampling technique based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Primary data were obtained from blood plasma samples examined using the immunochromatographic method (rapid test) according to standard operating procedures. Data were analyzed using descriptive methods to describe the frequency distribution of reactive and non-reactive results for HBsAg and Anti-HCV testing. This study was conducted at the Laboratory of Manding Public Health Center, Sumenep Regency, from February 1–28, 2026. The results showed that among 32 respondents, all obtained non-reactive HBsAg results (100%) and all Anti-HCV results were also non-reactive (100%). ABSTRAK Hepatitis B dan Hepatitis C masih menjadi masalah kesehatan masyarakat yang berpotensi menyebabkan komplikasi serius pada ibu hamil maupun janin, serta dapat ditularkan secara vertikal dari ibu ke bayi. Deteksi dini melalui pemeriksaan laboratorium pada masa kehamilan sangat penting dilakukan sebagai upaya pencegahan penularan serta penanganan yang optimal. Penelitian bertujuan untuk mengetahui gambaran hasil pemeriksaan Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg) dan Antibodi Hepatitis C Virus (Anti-HCV) pada ibu hamil di Puskesmas Manding, Kabupaten Sumenep. Sampel penelitian terdiri dari 32 ibu hamil trimester I dan II yang menjalani pemeriksaan laboratorium di Puskesmas Manding, pengambilan sampel dilakukan menggunakan teknik purposive sampling berdasarkan kriteria inklusi dan ekslusi. Data primer diperoleh dari plasma darah yang diperiksa menggunakan metode immunokromatografi (rapid test) sesuai standar operasional prosedur. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan metode deskriptif untuk menggambarkan distribusi frekuensi hasil reaktif dan non-reaktif pada pemeriksaan HBsAg dan Anti-HCV. Penelitian dilaksanakan di Laboratorium Puskesmas Manding Kabupaten Sumenep pada periode 1-28 Februari 2026. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa dari 32 responden, seluruhnya mendapatkan hasil HBsAg non-reaktif (100%) dan hasil Anti-HCV non-reaktif (100%).

papers.title: [A survey on knowledge, attitude, practice, and vaccination willingness regarding hepatitis B among students in a college in Dezhou City, 2026].
papers.abstract: A census-based questionnaire survey was conducted among all students enrolled in a college in Dezhou City in March 2026. The results showed that the overall qualified rate of hepatitis B-related knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) among 1 334 students was 29.16%, with the qualified rates for knowledge, attitude, and practice being 29.46% (393 students), 39.28% (524 students), and 39.66% (529 students), respectively. The overall willingness rate for hepatitis B vaccination was 37.93% (506 students). Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that, compared with medical students, non-medical students were less likely to have qualified KAP (OR=0.540, 95%CI: 0.354-0.826). Compared with heterosexual students, bisexual students (OR=0.207, 95%CI: 0.059-0.722) and students with uncertain sexual orientation (OR=0.275, 95%CI: 0.165-0.457) were less likely to have qualified KAP. Compared with students who had completed full-dose vaccination, those with partial-dose vaccination (OR=0.122, 95%CI: 0.046-0.322), unvaccinated students (OR=0.281, 95%CI: 0.168-0.468), and students with unknown vaccination history (OR=0.241, 95%CI: 0.180-0.323) were less likely to have qualified KAP. Compared with heterosexual students, students with uncertain sexual orientation showed lower willingness to receive hepatitis B vaccination (OR=0.649, 95%CI: 0.430-0.978). Students with unqualified KAP scores were less willing to receive hepatitis B vaccination than those with qualified scores (OR=0.097, 95%CI: 0.073-0.128).
papers.journal: Zhonghua yu fang yi xue za zhi [Chinese journal of preventive medicine]

papers.title: Hepatitis B Immunization Among Healthcare Students: A Narrative Review of Occupational Risk, Seroprotection, and Immunization Management
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Healthcare students face an occupational risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) exposure during clinical training, often many years after receiving their primary vaccination series in infancy or childhood. Progressive waning of anti-hepatitis B surface (anti-HBs) antibody titres, heterogeneous vaccination histories in international student cohorts, high rates of underreported needlestick injuries, and variable occupational health protocols across institutions raise important questions about the adequacy of pre-clinical immunization surveillance in this population. This review aimed to synthesize current evidence on hepatitis B immunization among healthcare students, focusing on occupational exposure risk, seroprotection and immunological memory, clinical management of low or absent anti-HB titres including post-exposure prophylaxis, and the specific challenges posed by multicultural academic settings. Methods: A narrative review was conducted through a systematic literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus, covering publications from January 2000 to December 2025, supplemented by key seminal references. After the removal of duplicates and stepwise screening, 49 references were selected for final inclusion. Results: Needlestick and sharps injuries occur at measurable rates during clinical training, with medical students accounting for approximately 30% of occupational exposure events in some series, and with underreporting rates estimated at 19–80% across studies. Pooled seroprotection prevalence at clinical training entry is approximately 73.8% (95% CI 69.1–78.0%), with substantially lower rates among students vaccinated in infancy—as low as 28% at 16–20 years post-vaccination in longitudinal data—compared with adolescence immunization. The majority of students with non-protective titres retain immunological memory, with 90.9% (95% CI 87.7–93.3%) demonstrating an anamnestic response after a single booster dose. Post-exposure prophylaxis pathways depend critically on pre-existing immunological status, reinforcing the operational value of pre-clinical serological screening. International student cohorts present additional complexity due to heterogeneous vaccination schedules, documentation gaps, and variable natural immunity profiles. Conclusions: Systematic pre-clinical serological screening (anti-HBs, HBsAg, and anti-HBc), combined with evidence-based stepwise immunization management and structured educational interventions, is essential to protect healthcare students from occupational HBV exposure. The primary operational goal of screening is the identification of the approximately 5% of true non-responders who require tailored occupational health management. These findings support a proactive, integrated approach to hepatitis B immunization surveillance in healthcare education, aligned with the WHO 2030 viral hepatitis-elimination targets.

papers.title_zh: 医疗保健学生的乙型肝炎免疫接种:职业风险、血清保护和免疫管理的叙述性回顾
papers.source_body_en: Background/Objectives: Healthcare students face an occupational risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) exposure during clinical training, often many years after receiving their primary vaccination series in infancy or childhood. Progressive waning of anti-hepatitis B surface (anti-HBs) antibody titres, heterogeneous vaccination histories in international student cohorts, high rates of underreported needlestick injuries, and variable occupational health protocols across institutions raise important questions about the adequacy of pre-clinical immunization surveillance in this population. This review aimed to synthesize current evidence on hepatitis B immunization among healthcare students, focusing on occupational exposure risk, seroprotection and immunological memory, clinical management of low or absent anti-HB titres including post-exposure prophylaxis, and the specific challenges posed by multicultural academic settings. Methods: A narrative review was conducted through a systematic literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus, covering publications from January 2000 to December 2025, supplemented by key seminal references. After the removal of duplicates and stepwise screening, 49 references were selected for final inclusion. Results: Needlestick and sharps injuries occur at measurable rates during clinical training, with medical students accounting for approximately 30% of occupational exposure events in some series, and with underreporting rates estimated at 19–80% across studies. Pooled seroprotection prevalence at clinical training entry is approximately 73.8% (95% CI 69.1–78.0%), with substantially lower rates among students vaccinated in infancy—as low as 28% at 16–20 years post-vaccination in longitudinal data—compared with adolescence immunization. The majority of students with non-protective titres retain immunological memory, with 90.9% (95% CI 87.7–93.3%) demonstrating an anamnestic response after a single booster dose. Post-exposure prophylaxis pathways depend critically on pre-existing immunological status, reinforcing the operational value of pre-clinical serological screening. International student cohorts present additional complexity due to heterogeneous vaccination schedules, documentation gaps, and variable natural immunity profiles. Conclusions: Systematic pre-clinical serological screening (anti-HBs, HBsAg, and anti-HBc), combined with evidence-based stepwise immunization management and structured educational interventions, is essential to protect healthcare students from occupational HBV exposure. The primary operational goal of screening is the identification of the approximately 5% of true non-responders who require tailored occupational health management. These findings support a proactive, integrated approach to hepatitis B immunization surveillance in healthcare education, aligned with the WHO 2030 viral hepatitis-elimination targets.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景/目标:医疗保健学生在临床培训期间面临 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 暴露的职业风险,通常是在婴儿期或儿童期接受主要 疫苗接种 系列多年后。抗乙型肝炎表面(抗 HBs)抗体滴度逐渐下降、国际学生 队列研究 的异质 疫苗接种 病史、漏报的针刺伤率较高,以及各机构不同的职业健康方案,这些都引发了有关该人群临床前免疫 监测 是否充分的重要问题。本综述旨在综合医疗保健学生乙型肝炎免疫的最新证据,重点关注职业暴露风险、血清保护和免疫记忆、抗-HB滴度低或缺失的临床管理(包括暴露后预防)以及多元文化学术环境带来的具体挑战。方法:通过 PubMed/MEDLINE 和 Scopus 的系统文献检索进行叙述性综述,涵盖 2000 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月的出版物,并辅以重要的开创性参考文献。经过去重复和逐步筛选后,最终选出 49 篇参考文献纳入。结果:在临床培训期间,针刺伤和锐器伤的发生率是可测量的,在一些系列中,医科生约占职业暴露事件的 30%,并且各项研究中漏报率估计为 19-80%。进入临床培训时,患病率 的汇总血清保护率约为 73.8%(95% CI 69.1-78.0%),与青春期免疫相比,婴儿期接种疫苗的学生的比率要低得多,纵向数据显示,疫苗接种 接种后 16-20 岁时,该比率低至 28%。大多数具有非保护性滴度的学生保留了免疫记忆,其中 90.9% (95% CI 87.7–93.3%) 在单次加强剂量后表现出记忆反应。暴露后预防途径主要取决于预先存在的免疫学状态,增强了临床前血清学筛查的操作价值。由于不同的 队列研究 时间表、文档差距和可变的自然免疫特征,国际学生 队列研究 呈现出额外的复杂性。结论:系统的临床前血清学筛查(抗 HBs、HBsAg 和抗 HBc),结合循证的逐步免疫管理和结构化教育干预措施,对于保护医护人员免受职业性 HBV 暴露至关重要。筛查的主要操作目标是识别大约 5% 的真正无反应者,他们需要量身定制的职业健康管理。这些发现支持在医疗保健教育中采取积极、综合的乙型肝炎免疫 监测 方法,与世界卫生组织 2030 年病毒性肝炎消除目标保持一致。

papers.title: Characterising Hepatitis D Virus in the UK From 2011 to 2021.
papers.abstract: Little is known about hepatitis B virus (HBV) and Hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection in the UK. HDV screening is recommended among all individuals with HBV, with coinfection associated with increased disease progression. Using data on HDV testing, shared by 11 laboratories in the UK who reported undertaking HDV testing, and national testing data for HBV we established a cohort of individuals tested for HDV, investigating testing pathways, describing characteristics and outcomes of those HDV-RNA positive to inform targeted interventions for testing, diagnosis and linkage to care. Demographic information, clinical assessments, treatment and recent laboratory results from NHS trusts, and through linkage to national healthcare datasets was collected for HDV-RNA positive individuals. Between 2011 and 2021, 42% of individuals newly diagnosed with HBV in England were linked to an HDV test. Anti-HDV positivity was 5.0%, 55.8% were HDV-RNA tested and 45.7% were ever HDV-RNA positive. HDV-RNA positivity in the absence of an anti-HDV result was 6.4%. Among individuals who were HDV-RNA positive, 94.3% were non-UK born, with 24 different primary languages reported, 49% had evidence of treatment, and 48% had evidence of cirrhosis. 10% had died of which 58.4% died of liver disease. In conclusion, our findings indicate that HDV testing in HBV positive individuals in the UK is sub-optimal against testing guidelines, including RNA testing among those who are anti-HDV positive. Considerable work is needed to improve the patient care pathway, to ensure patients are appropriately diagnosed, linked and retained in care, with adequate access to treatment.

papers.title_zh: 2011 年至 2021 年英国丁型肝炎病毒的特征。
papers.source_body_en: Little is known about hepatitis B virus (HBV) and Hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection in the UK. HDV screening is recommended among all individuals with HBV, with coinfection associated with increased disease progression. Using data on HDV testing, shared by 11 laboratories in the UK who reported undertaking HDV testing, and national testing data for HBV we established a cohort of individuals tested for HDV, investigating testing pathways, describing characteristics and outcomes of those HDV-RNA positive to inform targeted interventions for testing, diagnosis and linkage to care. Demographic information, clinical assessments, treatment and recent laboratory results from NHS trusts, and through linkage to national healthcare datasets was collected for HDV-RNA positive individuals. Between 2011 and 2021, 42% of individuals newly diagnosed with HBV in England were linked to an HDV test. Anti-HDV positivity was 5.0%, 55.8% were HDV-RNA tested and 45.7% were ever HDV-RNA positive. HDV-RNA positivity in the absence of an anti-HDV result was 6.4%. Among individuals who were HDV-RNA positive, 94.3% were non-UK born, with 24 different primary languages reported, 49% had evidence of treatment, and 48% had evidence of cirrhosis. 10% had died of which 58.4% died of liver disease. In conclusion, our findings indicate that HDV testing in HBV positive individuals in the UK is sub-optimal against testing guidelines, including RNA testing among those who are anti-HDV positive. Considerable work is needed to improve the patient care pathway, to ensure patients are appropriately diagnosed, linked and retained in care, with adequate access to treatment.

papers.title: Seroprevalence of Hepatitis B Virus and Hepatitis C Virus Coinfection in People Living with HIV at the Al Nadjma Multipurpose Center in N'Djamena, Chad
papers.abstract: Introduction: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), Hepatitis B Virus (HBV), and Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) are all bloodborne viruses that share similar routes of transmission. People with HIV who become infected with HBV or HCV are at increased risk of liver-related morbidity and mortality, which are common in our region. Chad is part of sub-Saharan Africa, which is a highly endemic region. Objective: The objective of this study was to assess the seroprevalence of HIV-HBV and HIV-HCV coinfection in patients at the Al Nadjma Multipurpose Center in N'Djamena, Chad. Patients and Methods: This was a cross-sectional, descriptive study with prospective data collection over a 12-month period from 1 January to 31 December 2023. Data were entered using Microsoft Word and analysed using SPSS software. We obtained informed consent from all individuals screened. Data confidentiality was maintained in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki. Results: Of the 1,000 patients with HIV who were followed during the study period, 76 patients were coinfected with HBV (7.6%), 8 patients with HCV (0.8%), and 4 patients with both HBV and HCV (0.4%). The mean age of the patients was 33 ±5 years. There was a male predominance, with a sex ratio of 1.05. Having multiple sexual partners was the most frequent risk factor, reported by 21.3% (n=17). Merchants were the most represented occupational group, accounting for 25% (n=20), and married individuals accounted for 47.5% (n=38). Patients who had entered the voluntary HIV testing programme represented 96.2% (n=77). Body mass index was normal in 62.5% (n=50) of patients. Fever was the most frequent symptom, reported in 51% (n=41) of patients, and 63.8% (n=51) of patients were at WHO clinical stage 1. All patients were infected with HIV type 1. Virologically, after 6 months of antiretroviral therapy, the viral load was undetectable in 75% (n=60) of patients, and at 12 months, all patients had an undetectable viral load. Blood tests revealed moderate anaemia in 12.5% (n=10) of patients and leukopenia in 6.3% (n=5), while platelet counts were normal in all patients. Biochemical tests showed elevated transaminases in 33.33% (n=5) of patients, and renal function tests were normal in all patients. Abdominal ultrasound, performed in 6.2% (n=5) of patients, was normal. Conclusion: In this study, the seroprevalence of HBV and HCV was low in people living with HIV compared with the general population; however, this reflects the substantial burden of HIV-HBV and HIV-HCV coinfection in the country and highlights the importance of systematic screening for early patient management.

papers.title: Mapping Hepatitis B Virus Research and Genomic Diversity in Latin America and the Caribbean
papers.abstract: Background: Hepatitis B (HBV) infection remains a major public health challenge in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC), a region characterized by disparities in re-search capacity and limited molecular surveillance. A comprehensive assessment of research output and viral genetic diversity is crucial for informing region-specific control strategies. Methods: An integrated analysis combining bibliometrics, text-mining, and genomics was performed on HBV-related publications indexed in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (1970–2024), along with 9,528 HBV nucleotide sequences from GenBank. Results: The study identified 4,083 publications, of which 72.1% (2,942) originated from Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina. Most were original articles (75.8%; 2,749/3,628) and involved human subjects (95.8%; 2,471/2,580), with a primary focus on serological markers, co-infections, vaccination, genotype characterization, liver pathology, and transfusion safety. Conversely, hepatocellular carcinoma, antiviral therapy, and met-abolic comorbidities were notably underrepresented. In vitro studies were limited, primarily examining viral replication, disease mechanisms, and gene expression, whereas animal studies focused on vaccine development, infection dynamics, and immune responses. Phylogenetic analysis identified eight circulating HBV genotypes (A–H), with genotypes A (43.4%; 4,138/9,528), F (29.3%; 2,787/9,528), and D (19.8%; 1,885/9,528) predominating. Genotype H was found mainly in Mexico (3.2%; 306/9,528). Notably, non-A genotypes accounted for most infections and showed dis-tinct geographic clustering (p < 0.001). Conclusion: HBV research in LAC is marked by pronounced regional disparities in scientific output, critical gaps in experimental and clinical research, and high viral di-versity. These findings underscore the need to strengthen regional research capacity and develop targeted strategies for HBV prevention, treatment, and vaccination to achieve hepatitis B elimination in the region.

papers.title: Functionally cured chronic hepatitis B: A cure‐related occult HBV infection state
papers.abstract: Abstract Occult HBV infection (OBI) is characterized by the presence of replication‐competent hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA (covalently closed circular DNA [cccDNA] and/or relaxed circular DNA [rcDNA]) in the liver and/or HBV DNA in the blood, despite negative hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) serology. The potential risks associated with OBI include HBV blood transmission, diagnostic challenges, and viral reactivation under immunosuppressive therapy. Some patients with OBI may face a higher risk of liver fibrosis compared to those who have achieved complete clearance of the virus. Functional cure is defined as the clearance of HBsAg, with or without hepatitis B surface antibody (anti‐HBs) seroconversion, and undetectable serum HBV DNA after finite therapy. It has been recommended as the optimal goal of antiviral treatment for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) by major guidelines. We highlight that patients achieving functional cure represent a distinct form of cure‐related OBI, with unique virological features and potential clinical implications. Furthermore, although direct epidemiological evidence remains limited, accumulating studies have demonstrated that OBI cases with undetectable HBV DNA and negative HBsAg serology retain the potential for transfusion transmission. Accordingly, the transfusion‐related risk associated with functional cure should not be overlooked. Here, we discuss the definition, virological and immunological basis, prevalence, diagnosis, and clinical significance of OBI, highlighting its link to cccDNA persistence and immune suppression of viral replication. Finally, we emphasize regular follow‐up to mitigate the risks of transfusion‐related transmission, HBV reactivation, and disease progression. Further research is warranted to elucidate the viral and immune status of functionally cured patients, thereby optimizing treatment strategies and ensuring blood safety.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the concept of functional cure in chronic hepatitis B and its association with occult HBV infection, highlighting the need to understand the virological and clinical implications of this state.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of existing literature and clinical observations, focusing on patients with chronic hepatitis B who have achieved functional cure, defined as HBsAg clearance with undetectable HBV DNA levels.
analysis.methods: The authors reviewed published studies and clinical data to define functional cure, discuss its virological and immunological basis, and analyze its prevalence, diagnosis, and clinical significance.
analysis.main_results: The study found that some patients with occult HBV infection may have a higher risk of liver fibrosis compared to those with complete viral clearance, and that OBI cases with undetectable HBV DNA and negative HBsAg serology can still pose transfusion-related risks.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that functional cure represents a unique form of cure-related OBI, with distinct virological features and potential clinical implications, emphasizing the need for further research to optimize treatment strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of regular follow-up for functionally cured patients to mitigate risks of transfusion transmission, HBV reactivation, and disease progression, contributing to improved surveillance and blood safety protocols.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on existing literature and does not include direct epidemiological evidence, which limits the strength of its conclusions. However, the evidence is consistent with accumulating studies on OBI and functional cure.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the concept of functional cure in chronic hepatitis B, defined as HBsAg clearance with undetectable HBV DNA levels. It highlights that functional cure may represent a distinct form of cure-related occult HBV infection (OBI), with unique virological features and potential clinical implications. The authors emphasize the importance of understanding OBI's link to cccDNA persistence and immune suppression, as well as the need for regular follow-up to mitigate risks of transfusion transmission, HBV reactivation, and disease progression. While the study is based on existing literature and lacks direct epidemiological evidence, it contributes to the growing body of knowledge on OBI and its management. The findings suggest that functional cure should not be overlooked in terms of its associated risks, and further research is needed to optimize treatment strategies and ensure blood safety.

papers.title_zh: 功能性治愈 慢性乙型肝炎:与治愈相关的隐匿性 HBV 感染状态
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Occult HBV infection (OBI) is characterized by the presence of replication‐competent hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA (covalently closed circular DNA [cccDNA] and/or relaxed circular DNA [rcDNA]) in the liver and/or HBV DNA in the blood, despite negative hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) serology. The potential risks associated with OBI include HBV blood transmission, diagnostic challenges, and viral reactivation under immunosuppressive therapy. Some patients with OBI may face a higher risk of liver fibrosis compared to those who have achieved complete clearance of the virus. Functional cure is defined as the clearance of HBsAg, with or without hepatitis B surface antibody (anti‐HBs) seroconversion, and undetectable serum HBV DNA after finite therapy. It has been recommended as the optimal goal of antiviral treatment for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) by major guidelines. We highlight that patients achieving functional cure represent a distinct form of cure‐related OBI, with unique virological features and potential clinical implications. Furthermore, although direct epidemiological evidence remains limited, accumulating studies have demonstrated that OBI cases with undetectable HBV DNA and negative HBsAg serology retain the potential for transfusion transmission. Accordingly, the transfusion‐related risk associated with functional cure should not be overlooked. Here, we discuss the definition, virological and immunological basis, prevalence, diagnosis, and clinical significance of OBI, highlighting its link to cccDNA persistence and immune suppression of viral replication. Finally, we emphasize regular follow‐up to mitigate the risks of transfusion‐related transmission, HBV reactivation, and disease progression. Further research is warranted to elucidate the viral and immune status of functionally cured patients, thereby optimizing treatment strategies and ensuring blood safety.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 隐匿性 HBV 感染 (OBI) 的特点是肝脏中存在有复制能力的 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) DNA(共价闭合环状 DNA [共价闭合环状DNA] 和/或松弛环状 DNA [rcDNA])和/或血液中存在 HBV DNA,尽管乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 血清学 呈阴性。与 OBI 相关的潜在风险包括 HBV 血液 传播、诊断挑战以及免疫抑制治疗下病毒再激活。与病毒完全清除的患者相比,一些 OBI 患者可能面临更高的肝纤维化风险。功能性治愈 定义为 HBsAg 清除率,有或没有乙型肝炎表面抗体(抗 HBs)血清转换,且有限治疗后血清 HBV DNA 检测不到。已被主要指南推荐为慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)的抗病毒药物 治疗的最佳目标。我们强调,达到 功能性治愈 的患者代表了一种与治愈相关的 OBI 的独特形式,具有独特的病毒学特征和潜在的临床意义。此外,尽管直接流行病学证据仍然有限,但不断积累的研究表明,HBV DNA 检测不到且 HBsAg 传播 阴性的 OBI 病例保留了输血 传播 的潜力。因此,与 功能性治愈 相关的输血相关风险不应被忽视。在这里,我们讨论 OBI 的定义、病毒学和免疫学基础、患病率、诊断 和临床意义,强调其与 共价闭合环状DNA 持久性和病毒复制免疫抑制的联系。最后,我们强调定期随访,以降低输血相关的 传播、HBV 再激活和疾病进展的风险。需要进一步的研究来阐明功能性治愈患者的病毒和免疫状态,从而优化 治疗 策略并确保血液安全。

papers.title: Targeting cccDNA for Degradation: Endogenous- and Exogenous-Based Methods of Nuclear-Localized DNA Destruction in the Context of Chronic Hepatitis B Infection
papers.abstract: The ability to facilitate cellular degradation or achieve therapeutic destruction of targeted noxious DNA is recognized as a major goal for the treatment of various viral infections. In the case of chronic hepatitis B, targeted DNA degradation of the episomal viral genome found in the nucleus of infected hepatocytes is key to achieving a true cure. However, mechanisms of targeted DNA degradation without excessive broadscale cytotoxicity are still under investigation by researchers. This review summarizes several current systems known to have the ability to target nuclear-localized DNA, including endogenous methods of DNA degradation that may be harnessed therapeutically and exogenous methods such as CRISPR or other xenobiotics, with a focus on their potential application in hepatitis B treatment.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述的重点是开发靶向和降解核定位 DNA 的方法,特别是在 慢性乙型肝炎 感染的情况下。核心问题是内源性或外源性系统是否可以在不引起过度细胞毒性的情况下实现对受感染肝细胞中附加型病毒 基因组 的治疗性破坏。

papers.title: The Impact of Chronic Hepatitis D Virus Infection on Health-Related Quality of Life and Fatigue: A Real-World International Study.
papers.abstract: As little is known about the disease burden of chronic hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection, this study examined health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and fatigue at different disease stages. This was a real-world quantitative cross-sectional survey of patients in Germany, Italy, Spain and the USA. Patients were recruited via their treating physicians. Patients who had received bulevirtide for hepatitis B or treatment licensed for HDV were excluded. Of 211 patients, 41% were noncirrhotic (F0-F3); 20% had liver cirrhosis with normal function (compensated); 20% had liver cirrhosis (F4) with impaired function (decompensated); 19% had hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Mean (standard deviation; SD) age was 54.5 (11.5) years, 75% were male. ANOVA showed a significant decrease (indicating poorer HRQoL) in EQ-5D-3L visual analogue scale (VAS) scores and index values with worsening disease stage and increasing severity (all p < 0.0001). All domain scores of the Hepatitis Quality of Life Questionnaire v2 (except positive wellbeing) worsened with progressing disease and increasing symptom severity (all p ≤ 0.0001). Mean Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS) total scores also increased, indicating greater fatigue, with worsening of disease and increasing symptom severity (both p < 0.0001). HDV infection significantly impacts patients' HRQoL and fatigue, particularly for patients at later disease stages. Treatments that slow disease progression, reducing the burden of HDV infection, are needed.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是对德国、意大利、西班牙和美国患者的真实世界定量横断面调查。患者是通过治疗医生招募的,在 211 名患者中,41% 为非肝硬化 (F0-F3);20%患有肝硬化但功能正常(代偿);20% 患有肝硬化(F4)且功能受损(失代偿);19% 患有肝细胞癌 (HCC)。
elements_zh.methods: 采用方差分析分析不同疾病阶段的 EQ-5D-3L 视觉模拟量表 (VAS) 评分和指数值、肝炎生活质量问卷 v2 领域评分以及疲劳严重程度量表 (FSS) 总分。

papers.title: Immune correlates of outcomes after nucleos(t)ide analogue withdrawal in chronic hepatitis B: direct evidence, mechanistic context, and candidate biomarkers
papers.abstract: Nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) discontinuation in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) can produce two clinically divergent trajectories: a minority of patients achieve sustained hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss or off-treatment viral control, whereas others develop hepatitis flares without virological benefit. Recent longitudinal studies have begun to define the host immune correlates of these outcomes. This Mini Review separates direct evidence from NA-withdrawal cohorts from mechanistic evidence obtained in other CHB settings. Direct human data suggest that beneficial outcomes are associated with recovery of HBsAg-specific memory B-cell activity, plasmablast expansion, stronger T follicular helper collaboration, and preserved hepatitis B virus (HBV)-specific T-cell function. In contrast, high inhibitory-receptor expression on global T cells, persistent inflammatory chemokine signatures, and greater post-flare alanine aminotransferase variability are associated with non-beneficial flares. immune complexes formed by HBsAg and antibodies to HBsAg provide an additional humoral readout that may reflect both flare risk and the quality of HBsAg decline. These observations are promising but remain exploratory: cohorts are small, flare definitions are heterogeneous, assays are not standardized, and most signatures lack external validation. Immune markers should therefore be viewed as candidate correlates to be integrated with viral biomarkers, liver-disease severity, and close post-withdrawal monitoring rather than as stand-alone criteria for stopping therapy.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores immune correlates of outcomes following nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) withdrawal in chronic hepatitis B (CHB). It highlights that NA discontinuation can lead to two distinct clinical outcomes: some patients achieve sustained HBsAg loss or viral control, while others experience hepatitis flares. Direct human evidence suggests that beneficial outcomes are linked to immune markers such as HBsAg-specific memory B-cell activity, plasmablast expansion, T follicular helper collaboration, and preserved HBV-specific T-cell function. Conversely, non-beneficial flares are associated with high inhibitory-receptor expression, persistent inflammatory chemokine signatures, and variability in alanine aminotransferase levels. However, the findings remain exploratory due to small cohorts, heterogeneous flare definitions, non-standardized assays, and lack of external validation. The review emphasizes that immune markers should be considered as candidate correlates to be used alongside viral biomarkers, liver disease severity, and close monitoring rather than as standalone criteria for stopping therapy.

papers.title: Hepatitis-B virus reactivation during Immunosuppressive therapy: Clinical observations from a tertiary care center
papers.abstract: Objectives: This study evaluated the incidence of hepatitis B virus reactivation (HBVr) in patients receiving immunosuppressive therapy and examined the association between anti-HBs titers and reactivation risk in routine clinical practice. Methods: This retrospective study was conducted at Düzce University Faculty of Medicine Hospital between 2017 and 2020. Adult patients (≥18 years) receiving immunosuppressive therapy and monitored for HBVr were included. A total of 166 patients who were either HBsAg-positive or HBsAg-negative with anti-HBc positivity were analyzed. Demographic and clinical characteristics, type of immunosuppressive therapy, antiviral prophylaxis use, HBV serological markers, HBV DNA levels, and HBVr episodes were obtained from medical records. Patients were categorized into three groups according to serological status and prophylaxis use. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 22.0, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Results: The mean age of the cohort was 54 ± 12.7 years, and 42.1% were male. Most patients were HBsAg-negative/anti-HBc–positive (90.4%), while 9.6% were HBsAg-positive. Antiviral prophylaxis was administered to 37.3% of patients. HBVr occurred in 17.3% of HBsAg-negative patients without prophylaxis and was significantly more frequent in those with anti-HBs titers <100 mIU/mL than in those with titers ≥100 mIU/mL (p = 0.049). Among HBsAg-negative patients receiving prophylaxis, HBVr was observed in 8.7%. Only one HBVr episode occurred among HBsAg-positive patients receiving prophylaxis. Conclusion: HBVr risk during immunosuppressive therapy is shaped by HBsAg status, antiviral prophylaxis, and anti-HBs titers. Prophylaxis markedly reduces risk, while anti-HBs titers ≥100 mIU/mL provide additional protection and may guide individualized prophylaxis strategies.

papers.abstract: Gender differences in disease burden are often overlooked in public health programming, despite their critical role in shaping infection dynamics and healthcare access. This study explores gender-based disparities in Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) prevalence in Kaura Namoda, Zamfara State, Nigeria, between 2019 and 2023. Using secondary data obtained from the HBV screening records of Kaura Namoda General Hospital, the study analyzed the distribution of confirmed HBV cases across male and female populations over five years. Descriptive statistics revealed that males consistently exhibited higher infection rates compared to females. This disparity is attributed to a combination of factors including occupational exposure, informal medical practices, low health-seeking behavior among men, and cultural barriers that deter male participation in preventive healthcare. Conversely, women benefited from integrated screening during antenatal care services, facilitating early detection and treatment. The findings mirror similar gender patterns reported in other parts of Northern Nigeria, indicating a systemic gap in HBV prevention and control strategies for men. To address these disparities, the study recommends gender-sensitive interventions such as mobile male-focused screening campaigns, workplace-based vaccination programs, and the engagement of traditional leaders to promote male participation in health services. Furthermore, gender-disaggregated data should be routinely collected to guide policy decisions and ensure equitable health outcomes. The study contributes to the growing body of evidence advocating for targeted health strategies that acknowledge and address gender-specific vulnerabilities in HBV transmission and prevention.

papers.abstract_zh: 疾病负担方面的性别差异在公共卫生规划中经常被忽视,尽管它们在影响感染动态和医疗保健获取方面发挥着关键作用。本研究探讨了 2019 年至 2023 年间尼日利亚扎姆法拉州 Kaura Namoda 的 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 患病率 中基于性别的差异。该研究利用从 Kaura Namoda 总医院的 HBV 筛查记录中获得的二手数据,分析了五年来男性和女性人群中确诊的 HBV 病例的分布情况。描述性统计数据显示,与女性相比,男性的感染率始终较高。这种差异是由多种因素造成的,包括职业暴露、非正式的医疗实践、男性寻求健康的行为较低以及阻碍男性参与预防性医疗保健的文化障碍。相反,妇女受益于产前保健服务期间的综合筛查,促进早期发现和 治疗。研究结果反映了尼日利亚北部其他地区报告的类似性别模式,表明男性乙型肝炎预防和控制策略存在系统性差距。为了解决这些差异,该研究建议采取对性别敏感的干预措施,例如以男性为中心的移动筛查活动、基于工作场所的 疫苗接种 计划以及传统领导人的参与,以促进男性参与卫生服务。此外,应定期收集按性别分列的数据,以指导政策决策并确保公平的健康结果。该研究提供了越来越多的证据,倡导制定有针对性的健康策略,承认并解决 HBV 传播 和预防中的性别特定脆弱性。

papers.title: Renal function and urinary tubular biomarker abnormalities in untreated and entecavir- or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate–treated patients with chronic hepatitis B: a retrospective cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Background Renal safety is an important consideration during nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) may affect proximal tubular function, while serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) primarily reflect glomerular filtration. This study compared glomerular-function measures and urinary tubular biomarker patterns among NA-untreated, entecavir (ETV)-treated, and TDF-treated patients with CHB. Methods This single-center retrospective cross-sectional study included 242 adults with CHB assessed between June 2025 and June 2026: 113 NA-untreated, 64 ETV-treated, and 65 TDF-treated participants. For treated participants, the single index assessment was obtained after at least 12 months of continuous corresponding monotherapy. Serum creatinine, eGFR, urinary α 1-microglobulin (A1M), urinary β 2-microglobulin (B2M), and urinary microalbumin (U-mAlb) were compared among groups. eGFR was calculated using the 2009 CKD-EPI creatinine equation and analyzed primarily as a continuous measure; eGFR 0.30 mg/L were 25.7%, 48.4%, and 75.4%. Both A1M and B2M concentration-threshold exceedance were more frequent in TDF-treated than ETV-treated participants (Bonferroni-adjusted P = 0.0108 and P = 0.0048, respectively), and continuous B2M was also higher with TDF (adjusted P = 0.0074). Median eGFR was 112.98 (102.47–119.36), 104.79 (92.08–112.39), and 104.47 (91.24–116.58) mL/min/1.73 m 2 , respectively (overall P = 0.0008). Both treated groups had lower continuous eGFR than the NA-untreated group, whereas serum creatinine, continuous eGFR, and the frequency of eGFR <90 mL/min/1.73 m 2 did not differ between ETV and TDF (all Bonferroni-adjusted P = 1.0000). Conclusion TDF-treated participants showed a more prominent urinary A1M/B2M concentration-based biomarker pattern than ETV-treated participants, whereas conventional glomerular-function measures did not differ between the two treated groups. These findings represent cross-sectional associations rather than evidence of treatment-induced renal injury. The absence of pretreatment and serial renal measurements, urinary creatinine normalization, and a complete proximal tubular dysfunction assessment requires cautious interpretation and prospective longitudinal confirmation.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 在核苷(酸)类似物(NA)治疗 慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)期间,肾脏安全性是一个重要的考虑因素。富马酸替诺福韦二吡呋酯(TDF)可能影响近端肾小管功能,而血清肌酐和估计肾小球滤过率(eGFR)主要反映肾小球滤过。本研究比较了未接受 NA 治疗、接受恩替卡韦 (ETV) 治疗和接受 TDF 治疗的慢性乙型肝炎患者的肾小球功能测量和尿管生物标志物模式。方法 这项单中心回顾性横断面研究纳入了 2025 年 6 月至 2026 年 6 月期间评估的 242 名慢性乙型肝炎成人:113 名未经 NA 治疗的参与者、64 名接受 ETV 治疗的参与者和 65 名接受 TDF 治疗的参与者。对于接受治疗的参与者,在至少12个月的连续相应单一治疗后获得单一指标评估。比较各组之间的血清肌酐、eGFR、尿α1-微球蛋白(A1M)、尿β2-微球蛋白(B2M)和尿微量白蛋白(U-mAlb)。eGFR 使用 2009 CKD-EPI 肌酐方程计算,并主要作为连续测量进行分析;eGFR 0.30 mg/L 分别为 25.7%、48.4% 和 75.4%。TDF 治疗组的 A1M 和 B2M 浓度阈值超出频率均高于 ETV 治疗组(分别经 Bonferroni 调整的 P = 0.0108 和 P = 0.0048),并且 TDF 治疗组的连续 B2M 也更高(调整后的 P = 0.0074)。中位 eGFR 分别为 112.98 (102.47–119.36)、104.79 (92.08–112.39) 和 104.47 (91.24–116.58) mL/min/1.73 m 2 (总体 P = 0.0008)。两个治疗组的连续 eGFR 均低于 NA 未治疗组,而 ETV 和 TDF 之间的血清肌酐、连续 eGFR 和 eGFR <90 mL/min/1.73 m 2 的频率没有差异(所有 Bonferroni 调整后的 P = 1.0000)。结论 TDF 治疗的参与者比 ETV 治疗的参与者表现出更显着的基于尿液 A1M/B2M 浓度的生物标志物模式,而传统肾小球功能测量在两个治疗组之间没有差异。这些发现代表了横断面关联,而不是 治疗 诱导肾损伤的证据。由于缺乏预处理和连续肾脏测量、尿肌酐正常化和完整的近端肾小管功能障碍评估,需要谨慎的解释和前瞻性纵向确认。

analysis_zh.main_results: TDF 治疗组的 A1M 和 B2M 浓度阈值超出频率均高于 ETV 治疗组(分别经 Bonferroni 调整的 P = 0.0108 和 P = 0.0048),并且 TDF 治疗组的连续 B2M 也更高(调整后的 P = 0.0074)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 与 ETV 治疗的参与者相比,TDF 治疗的参与者表现出更显着的基于尿液 A1M/B2M 浓度的生物标志物模式,而传统的肾小球功能测量在两个治疗组之间没有差异。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为接受 TDF 或 ETV 治疗 慢性乙型肝炎 的患者的肾功能监测提供信息,特别是通过使用尿管生物标志物。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于缺乏预处理和连续肾脏测量、尿肌酐正常化和完整的近端肾小管功能障碍评估,需要谨慎的解释和前瞻性纵向确认。

papers.title: Analysis and Control of Hepatitis B Virus Spread with Harmonic Mean Incidence and Vertical Transmission: A Compartmental Modeling Approach
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B (HBV) is a potentially fatal liver infection that remains a primary widespread disease around the globe, despite the availability of vaccinations, owing to ongoing obstacles such as vertical transmission and delayed treatment. In the present study, a compartmental mathematical model that accounts for the effects of vertical transmission and harmonic mean type incidence is put forward for the analysis of the transmission dynamics of HBV. The model's threshold behavior is investigated through the basic reproduction number $R_0$, and the qualitative dynamics around the disease-free and endemic equilibria are examined to establish conditions for their asymptotic local and global stability. To identify key epidemiological drivers, the global sensitivity analysis of the system is performed through the incorporation of Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) and Partial Rank Correlation Coefficient (PRCC) methodologies. We formulate the optimal control problem using Pontryagin's maximum principle. Effective strategies for diminishing the prevalence of HBV are emphasized through numerical simulations. Numerical simulations demonstrated that optimized control measures play a significant role in reducing the number of infected individuals and increasing the recovered population. In addition, we have characterized three distinct strategies for reducing infection and observed that each has limitations in eliminating infections. However, the simultaneous administration of treatment and vaccination is useful and effective for the reduction of HBV infection.

The model investigates threshold behavior through the basic reproduction number $R_0$ and examines the stability of disease-free and endemic equilibria. A global sensitivity analysis is conducted using Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) and Partial Rank Correlation Coefficient (PRCC) methodologies to identify key epidemiological drivers. Numerical simulations show that optimized control measures significantly reduce the number of infected individuals and increase the recovered population. The authors emphasize the importance of combining treatment and vaccination strategies for effective HBV reduction. While the study provides valuable insights into modeling HBV transmission, it primarily focuses on theoretical analysis and does not include empirical data. The evidence is strong for the model's framework and implications but limited in direct observational results.

papers.source_body_en: Hepatitis B (HBV) is a potentially fatal liver infection that remains a primary widespread disease around the globe, despite the availability of vaccinations, owing to ongoing obstacles such as vertical transmission and delayed treatment. In the present study, a compartmental mathematical model that accounts for the effects of vertical transmission and harmonic mean type incidence is put forward for the analysis of the transmission dynamics of HBV. The model's threshold behavior is investigated through the basic reproduction number $R_0$, and the qualitative dynamics around the disease-free and endemic equilibria are examined to establish conditions for their asymptotic local and global stability. To identify key epidemiological drivers, the global sensitivity analysis of the system is performed through the incorporation of Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) and Partial Rank Correlation Coefficient (PRCC) methodologies. We formulate the optimal control problem using Pontryagin's maximum principle. Effective strategies for diminishing the prevalence of HBV are emphasized through numerical simulations. Numerical simulations demonstrated that optimized control measures play a significant role in reducing the number of infected individuals and increasing the recovered population. In addition, we have characterized three distinct strategies for reducing infection and observed that each has limitations in eliminating infections. However, the simultaneous administration of treatment and vaccination is useful and effective for the reduction of HBV infection.
papers.abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎 (HBV) 是一种潜在致命的肝脏感染,尽管存在 疫苗接种,但由于垂直 传播 和延迟 治疗 等持续存在的障碍,它仍然是全球范围内广泛传播的主要疾病。在本研究中,提出了一个考虑垂直传播和调和平均类型发病率影响的分区数学模型,用于分析HBV的传播动力学。通过基本再生数 $R_0$ 研究模型的阈值行为,并检查无病和地方性平衡周围的定性动态,以确定其渐近局部和全局稳定性的条件。为了确定关键的流行病学驱动因素,通过结合拉丁超立方抽样 (LHS) 和偏秩相关系数 (PRCC) 方法对系统进行全局敏感性分析。我们使用 Pontryagin 极大值原理制定最优控制问题。通过数值模拟强调了减少 HBV 患病率 的有效策略。数值模拟表明,优化的控制措施在减少感染人数和增加康复人数方面发挥着重要作用。此外,我们还描述了三种不同的减少感染策略,并观察到每种策略在消除感染方面都有局限性。然而,同时施用治疗和疫苗接种对于减少HBV感染是有用且有效的。

papers.title: High cost of silence: Needlestick injuries and the persistence of hepatitis B virus risk among healthcare trainees
papers.abstract: The study by Jaho et al published in the World Journal of Virology highlights a compelling paradox in occupational health: While a robust 86.6% of 134 Albanian health sciences students demonstrate seroprotection (antibody to hepatitis B surface antigen ≥ 10 IU/L), a staggering 64.5% report at least one needlestick injury during training.This high prevalence of exposure is compounded by a culture of silence, with one-third of incidents remaining unreported.This editorial analyzes why high seroprotection rates should not lead to institutional complacency.It argues that the specific vulnerability observed among midwifery students and the lack of systematic post-vaccination serological testing represent critical system gaps.Instead of relying solely on historical vaccination records, institutions should adopt guideline-based strategies for assessing hepatitis B immune status before clinical exposure, while fostering non-punitive reporting pathways.Bridging the gap between immunological protection and clinical behaviour is essential to safeguard those at the frontline of care.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the paradox of high seroprotection rates among healthcare trainees against hepatitis B virus despite a high prevalence of needlestick injuries, highlighting the need for improved safety measures and awareness.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is an editorial analyzing data from a prior study involving 134 Albanian health sciences students, focusing on their hepatitis B seroprotection status and reported needlestick injuries during training.
analysis.methods: The editorial reviews existing data on seroprotection rates and needlestick injury prevalence among healthcare trainees, emphasizing the importance of assessing immune status before clinical exposure and promoting non-punitive reporting of incidents.
analysis.main_results: The study reports that 86.6% of the 134 Albanian health sciences students have seroprotection against hepatitis B virus, while 64.5% have experienced at least one needlestick injury during training, with one-third of these incidents remaining unreported.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The editorial interprets these findings as evidence of a critical system gap, arguing that high seroprotection rates should not lead to complacency and that institutions must adopt guideline-based strategies for immune status assessment and foster safer reporting environments.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of proactive immune status evaluation and incident reporting in healthcare training settings to mitigate the risk of hepatitis B virus transmission among vulnerable frontline workers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on a single study, which may limit generalizability, but the high seroprotection rate and injury prevalence are reported with specific percentages, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial examines the paradox of high hepatitis B seroprotection rates among healthcare trainees in Albania despite frequent needlestick injuries. It highlights the need for improved safety protocols and non-punitive reporting systems to address the risk of virus exposure. The study emphasizes that while immunological protection is present, institutional complacency remains a critical issue. The findings suggest that systematic immune status assessments before clinical exposure are essential to ensure safety. The editorial argues that fostering a culture of transparency and adherence to guidelines can help bridge the gap between protection and practice. However, the evidence is limited to a single study, which may affect generalizability, though the reported percentages provide a moderate level of confidence.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项社论,分析了之前一项涉及 134 名阿尔巴尼亚健康科学专业学生的研究数据,重点关注他们的乙型肝炎血清保护状态以及训练期间报告的针刺伤情况。
elements_zh.methods: 该社论回顾了医疗保健实习生中血清保护率和针刺伤 患病率 的现有数据,强调在临床暴露前评估免疫状态和促进事件非惩罚性报告的重要性。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了在医疗保健培训环境中进行主动免疫状态评估和事件报告的重要性,以降低弱势一线工作人员中 乙型肝炎病毒 传播 的风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该证据基于一项研究,这可能会限制普遍性,但以特定百分比报告了高血清保护率和损伤 患病率,支持适度的置信度评估。

papers.title: Hepatitis B Immunity Status Among Doctors: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a significant occupational hazard for healthcare workers, including doctors. Ensuring immunity against HBV is crucial to prevent transmission. Vaccine against HBV is widely popular and is included in the expanded program of universal immunization in infancy. Objectives: To assess the HBsAg and anti-HBs status among doctors and identify the proportion of non-immune individuals. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 100 doctors. Health care workers other than doctors were excluded. Blood samples were collected and tested for HBsAg and anti-HBs antibodies using CMIA (Chemiluminescent Microparticle Immunoassay). Results: Out of 100 doctors, 75% reported being vaccinated against HBV. However, 40% of those vaccinated did not receive the recommended booster dose. Serological testing revealed that 21% of the doctors were non-immune to HBV. Conclusion: This study highlights the need for improved vaccination strategies, regular serological testing, and enhanced infection control practices to protect doctors and patients from HBV transmission.
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

papers.title: Emergency Department-Based Screening and Linkage-to-Care for Hepatitis B, C, and D in a Referral Hospital in Barcelona, Spain: Reduction in Hepatitis C Prevalence After Five Years
papers.abstract: Background: Emergency Department (ED) viral hepatitis screening programs typically report short-term outcomes. We evaluated the medium-term impact of an ED-based screening for Hepatitis C (HCV), Hepatitis B (HBV), and Hepatitis D (HDV) viruses. Methods: Prospective opportunistic screening conducted between January 2020 and December 2024 at a referral hospital in Barcelona. Adults attending the ED were screened for HBV, HCV, and HDV. Positive cases were evaluated and linked to care when appropriate. To assess screening impact, HCV RNA and HBsAg prevalences were compared between 2020–2021 and 2023–2024 among participants aged ≤80 years. Results: Over five years, 39,532 individuals were screened: 220 (0.56%) had detectable HCV RNA, 234 (0.59%) HBsAg, and 4 HDV RNA. Of 110 patients with detectable HCV RNA eligible for linkage, 84 (76%) were treated and cured. Among 135 HBV-positive individuals eligible for linkage, 116 (86%) attended outpatient follow-up. HCV RNA prevalence significantly decreased (0.58% vs. 0.35%, p = 0.005), whereas HBsAg prevalence did not vary (0.7% vs. Conclusions: Sustained ED-based screening enabled the identification and linkage to care of several individuals with HBV and HCV. This strategy contributed to a reduction in HCV prevalence among ED attendees and supports opportunistic ED screening in viral hepatitis elimination goals.

Of HCV RNA-positive patients eligible for linkage, 76% were treated and cured, while 86% of HBV-positive individuals attended outpatient follow-up. papers.title: Seroprevalence, associated factors, and molecular detection of hepatitis B virus co-infection among HIV-positive adults in Okene, Nigeria
papers.abstract: Background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection constitutes an important clinical and public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa. Beyond the burden of co-existing viral infections, HBV/HIV co-infection may be associated with alterations in nutritional status, micronutrient availability, antioxidant capacity, and immune function, which may influence the clinical course of liver disease. Despite this dual burden, locally specific data on HBV co-infection prevalence, sociodemographic characteristics, risk factors, and molecular confirmation among HIV-positive patients in Kogi State remain limited. In addition, the potential contribution of nutrition and functional food- derived bioactive compounds to the health of individuals with HBV/HIV co-infection remains an area requiring further investigation. Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 90 consenting HIV-positive adult patients at Reference Hospital, Okene. HBV co-infection was assessed using HBsAg rapid immunochromatographic testing. Sociodemographic and HBV transmission-related exposure data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Molecular confirmation was performed by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) targeting the HBV surface (S) gene, with amplicons of approximately 640 bp resolved by agarose gel electrophoresis. Data were entered into Microsoft Excel and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 26.0. Categorical variables were summarized using frequencies and percentages, while HBV prevalence was calculated as the proportion of HBsAg-positive participants within the relevant population or category. papers.source_body_en: Background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection constitutes an important clinical and public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa. Beyond the burden of co-existing viral infections, HBV/HIV co-infection may be associated with alterations in nutritional status, micronutrient availability, antioxidant capacity, and immune function, which may influence the clinical course of liver disease. Despite this dual burden, locally specific data on HBV co-infection prevalence, sociodemographic characteristics, risk factors, and molecular confirmation among HIV-positive patients in Kogi State remain limited. In addition, the potential contribution of nutrition and functional food- derived bioactive compounds to the health of individuals with HBV/HIV co-infection remains an area requiring further investigation. Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 90 consenting HIV-positive adult patients at Reference Hospital, Okene. HBV co-infection was assessed using HBsAg rapid immunochromatographic testing. Sociodemographic and HBV transmission-related exposure data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Molecular confirmation was performed by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) targeting the HBV surface (S) gene, with amplicons of approximately 640 bp resolved by agarose gel electrophoresis. Data were entered into Microsoft Excel and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 26.0. Categorical variables were summarized using frequencies and percentages, while HBV prevalence was calculated as the proportion of HBsAg-positive participants within the relevant population or category. Fisher's exact test and the Fisher–Freeman–Halton exact test were used to assess associations involving categorical variables because of the small number of HBsAg-positive participants and small expected cell frequencies. Statistical significance was set at p

papers.title: Gambaran Pemeriksaan Screening Hepatitis B dan Hepatitis C pada Ibu Hamil dengan Metode Imunokromatografi di Puskesmas Sidoarjo
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B dan Hepatitis C adalah penyakit infeksi yang dapat ditularkan dari ibu kepada bayi, terutama selama proses kehamilan dan persalinan. Pemeriksaan skrining pada ibu hamil penting dilakukan sebagai upaya deteksi dini dan pencegahan penularan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk memperoleh gambaran hasil pemeriksaan skrining Hepatitis B dan Hepatitis C pada ibu hamil menggunakan metode imunokromatografi di Puskesmas Sidoarjo. Penelitian ini menggunakan desain deskriptif dengan pendekatan cross-sectional. Sampel penelitian terdiri atas 30 ibu hamil trimester I, II, dan III yang menjalani pemeriksaan antenatal care (ANC) di Puskesmas Sidoarjo. Pemeriksaan dilakukan menggunakan rapid test HBsAg dan Anti-HCV dengan metode imunokromatografi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa seluruh responden memperoleh hasil nonreaktif pada pemeriksaan Hepatitis B menggunakan rapid test HbsAg sebanyak 30 orang (100%) dan pemeriksaan Hepatitis C menggunakan rapid test Anti-HCV sebanyak 30 orang (100%). penelitian ini menunujukkan tidak ditemukan infeksi Hepatitis pada ibu hamil di Puskesmas Sidoarjo. Diharapkan peneliti lanjutan menggunakan metode pemeriksaan yang lebih akurat dan sensitif, seperti ELISA atau PCR.

papers.title: Challenges in the Management of Hepatitis B Among Children and Adolescents: A 10-Year Single-Center Experience
papers.abstract: Following successful neonatal HBV vaccination and perinatal screening, pediatric hepatitis B has become uncommon in Central Europe. However, migration and complex clinical scenarios are reshaping its epidemiology. We aimed to characterize the clinical course, disease phases, and treatment eligibility of children with HBV infection. This retrospective single-center study included patients aged 0 to <18 years referred to a tertiary pediatric infectious diseases center in Warsaw, Poland, between January 2016 and June 2026. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were analyzed, and patients were classified according to the 2025 EASL guidelines. Sixteen children were included. New referrals tripled from 2016–2020 (n = 3) to 2021–2026 (n = 9), and 50% were refugees, predominantly from Ukraine. Vertical transmission accounted for 44% of infections, whereas 25% were iatrogenic. According to the 2025 EASL criteria, 38% (6/16) of patients were unclassifiable. Occult HBV infection was identified in 31%, while only 13% (2/16) received analogue therapy because of restrictive national treatment criteria. One adolescent developed liver fibrosis (7.6 kPa), likely related to metabolic steatohepatitis. Contemporary pediatric HBV management might require adaptation to changing epidemiology, recognition of the limitations of adult-derived disease phase classifications, and prevention of HBV reactivation during immunosuppression.

papers.title_zh: 儿童和青少年乙型肝炎管理的挑战:10 年单中心经验
papers.source_body_en: Following successful neonatal HBV vaccination and perinatal screening, pediatric hepatitis B has become uncommon in Central Europe. However, migration and complex clinical scenarios are reshaping its epidemiology. We aimed to characterize the clinical course, disease phases, and treatment eligibility of children with HBV infection. This retrospective single-center study included patients aged 0 to <18 years referred to a tertiary pediatric infectious diseases center in Warsaw, Poland, between January 2016 and June 2026. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were analyzed, and patients were classified according to the 2025 EASL guidelines. Sixteen children were included. New referrals tripled from 2016–2020 (n = 3) to 2021–2026 (n = 9), and 50% were refugees, predominantly from Ukraine. Vertical transmission accounted for 44% of infections, whereas 25% were iatrogenic. According to the 2025 EASL criteria, 38% (6/16) of patients were unclassifiable. Occult HBV infection was identified in 31%, while only 13% (2/16) received analogue therapy because of restrictive national treatment criteria. One adolescent developed liver fibrosis (7.6 kPa), likely related to metabolic steatohepatitis. Contemporary pediatric HBV management might require adaptation to changing epidemiology, recognition of the limitations of adult-derived disease phase classifications, and prevention of HBV reactivation during immunosuppression.

papers.title: Prognostic biochemical surrogates of hepatic functional recovery for defining recompensation in hepatitis B virus-related cirrhosis
papers.abstract: Background & aims: Baveno VII recompensation criteria require stable improvement in liver function tests, however, the optimal definition of biochemical improvement remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the discriminatory and prognostic performance of Child-Turcotte-Pugh (CTP) score components (albumin, bilirubin, and international normalised ratio (INR)) to validate their clinical utility in decompensated hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related cirrhosis. Methods: This retrospective cohort study identified patients with HBV-related cirrhosis and prior hepatic decompensation from a territory-wide electronic healthcare database in Hong Kong. All achieved complete HBV DNA suppression and absence of decompensating events for at least 12 months. Results:871 patients were included (67.4 % male; median age 62.4 years; 65.7% with ascites; 60.4% achieved CTP-A recompensation). Over a median follow-up of 65.7 (IQR 30.7-109.6) months, 320 (36.7%) patients died and 274 (31.5%) developed re-decompensation. Albumin showed the highest discriminatory performance for mortality (integrated time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.729 [95% CI 0.693-0.766]), followed by INR (0.618 [95% CI 0.569-0.661]) and bilirubin (0.562 [95% CI 0.513-0.612]). Re-decompensation showed a similar pattern. In the multivariable model, albumin was the only independent factor for mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 0.910 [95% CI 0.891-0.929]), whereas all three parameters independently predicted re-decompensation. Five-year survival probability decreased from 81.6% for CTP A5 to 57.7% for A6 and 48.6% for B7-8, and from 84.3% for albumin ≥39 g/L to 75.7%, 57.6%, and 40.9% for albumin 35-<39 g/L, 28-≤35 g/L, and <28 g/L, respectively (both log-rank p<0.001). Conclusion:In patients with HBV-related cirrhosis achieving viral suppression and clinical recompensation, albumin was the strongest predictor of mortality and re-decompensation. Patients with CTP A5 at recompensation had the lowest risk of adverse outcomes.
