AusperBio Completes $120 Million Series C Financing to Advance AHB-137 Toward Potential Commercialization and Expand Next-Generation HBV Therapies PR Newswire Thu, 27 August 2026 at 8:00 pm GMT-4 5 min read Financing supports advancement of AHB-137 toward potential commercialization, including its Phase 3 registrational program and commercialization readiness Proceeds will also accelerate AHB-171 and next-generation combination approaches designed to advance functional cure for chronic hepatitis B Series C brings AusperBio's total capital raised to $360 million since 2024 SAN FRANCISCO, Aug. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AusperBio Therapeutics, Inc. and Ausper Biopharma Co., Ltd. (collectively "AusperBio" or the "Company"), a near-commercial biopharmaceutical company focused on developing targeted oligonucleotide therapeutics for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and other diseases, today announced the closing of its $120 million Series C financing. AusperBio The financing was led by a leading strategic investor, with participation from new investor RA Capital Management, L.P. ("RA Capital"), alongside continued support from AusperBio's existing investors, including HanKang Capital, Sherpa Capital, InnoPinnacle Fund, Qiming Venture Partners, YuanBio Venture Capital, and CDH Investments. With the completion of the Series C, AusperBio has raised $360 million since 2024, reflecting strong and sustained investor confidence in the potential of the Company's lead programs and differentiated oligonucleotide platforms. The financing will support the continued development of AHB-137, AusperBio's lead investigational ASO therapy for CHB, including its Phase 3 registrational program and commercialization readiness. Proceeds will also accelerate the development of AHB-171, the Company's investigational HBV siRNA candidate built on its proprietary Au-HALOTM targeted delivery platform, advance next-generation combination approaches for CHB, and further expand the Company's pipeline of targeted oligonucleotide therapeutics addressing significant unmet medical needs. "This financing represents an important inflection point for AusperBio as we advance AHB-137 toward potential commercialization while developing next-generation therapies for CHB," said Dr. Guofeng Cheng, co-founder and CEO of AusperBio. "We are grateful for the continued confidence of our existing investors and pleased to welcome RA Capital to AusperBio. We look forward to building on this momentum to advance our strategy toward functional cure and unlock new opportunities across our oligonucleotide platforms." Dr. Chris Yang, co-founder and CSO of AusperBio, added, "AHB-137 has demonstrated promising clinical activity in patients and has the potential to serve as a backbone therapy for functional cure of CHB. Our Med-OligoTM ASO, Au-HALOTM targeted delivery and siRNA discovery platforms enable complementary approaches designed to achieve deeper and more durable antiviral responses. This financing will enable us to further advance these platforms and build on their potential to generate differentiated targeted oligonucleotide therapies for CHB and other diseases with significant unmet medical needs." Story continues About AHB-137 AHB-137 is AusperBio's lead investigational unconjugated antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB), developed using the Company's proprietary Med-OligoTM ASO platform. AHB-137 is designed to suppress hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) production, inhibit viral DNA replication, and promote immune reactivation, with the goal of achieving a functional cure for CHB. AHB-137 has demonstrated promising clinical results and is currently being evaluated in a Phase 3 trial in China, following completion of a global Phase 1 study and multiple Phase 2 studies. The Company is advancing AHB-137 through a coordinated global development strategy toward potential commercialization. AHB-137 is an investigational product candidate and has not been approved by any regulatory authority. About AHB-171 AHB-171 is an investigational hepatocyte-targeted siRNA therapeutic candidate for the treatment of CHB that leverages AusperBio's proprietary Au-HALOTM liver-targeting delivery platform. AHB-171 is designed to selectively suppress viral gene expression and provide potent and sustained antiviral activity. As the first clinical candidate developed using the Au-HALOTM platform, AHB-171 is advancing the clinical validation of the Company's targeted delivery and siRNA capabilities and broadening the Company's differentiated HBV pipeline. AHB-171 is an investigational product candidate and has not been approved by any regulatory authority. About Chronic Hepatitis B Chronic hepatitis B remains a significant global health burden, affecting an estimated 254 million people worldwide and causing approximately 1.1 million deaths annually, primarily from cirrhosis and liver cancer, according to the World Health Organization. Current therapies can suppress viral replication but rarely achieve a functional cure, leaving many patients requiring long-term treatment. About AusperBio AusperBio is a near-commercial biopharmaceutical company focused on developing differentiated oligonucleotide therapeutics and targeted delivery technologies, with an initial focus on achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B. The Company's innovation engine is built on its proprietary Med-OligoTM ASO and Au-HALOTM targeted delivery platforms, supporting the development of therapies across multiple oligonucleotide modalities. With multiple clinical-stage programs and a growing pipeline, AusperBio is advancing a backbone-based combination strategy for functional cure of CHB while exploring opportunities in additional disease areas with significant unmet medical needs. AusperBio Completes $120 Million Series C Financing to Advance AHB-137 Toward Potential Commercialization and Expand Next-Generation HBV Therapies PR Newswire Thu, 27 August 2026 at 8:00 pm GMT-4 5 min read Financing supports advancement of AHB-137 toward potential commercialization, including its Phase 3 registrational program and commercialization readiness Proceeds will also accelerate AHB-171 and next-generation combination approaches designed to advance functional cure for chronic hepatitis B Series C brings AusperBio's total capital raised to $360 million since 2024 SAN FRANCISCO, Aug. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AusperBio Therapeutics, Inc. and Ausper Biopharma Co., Ltd. (collectively "AusperBio" or the "Company"), a near-commercial biopharmaceutical company focused on developing targeted oligonucleotide therapeutics for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and other diseases, today announced the closing of its $120 million Series C financing. AusperBio The financing was led by a leading strategic investor, with participation from new investor RA Capital Management, L.P. ("RA Capital"), alongside continued support from AusperBio's existing investors, including HanKang Capital, Sherpa Capital, InnoPinnacle Fund, Qiming Venture Partners, YuanBio Venture Capital, and CDH Investments. With the completion of the Series C, AusperBio has raised $360 million since 2024, reflecting strong and sustained investor confidence in the potential of the Company's lead programs and differentiated oligonucleotide platforms. The financing will support the continued development of AHB-137, AusperBio's lead investigational ASO therapy for CHB, including its Phase 3 registrational program and commercialization readiness. Proceeds will also accelerate the development of AHB-171, the Company's investigational HBV siRNA candidate built on its proprietary Au-HALOTM targeted delivery platform, advance next-generation combination approaches for CHB, and further expand the Company's pipeline of targeted oligonucleotide therapeutics addressing significant unmet medical needs. "This financing represents an important inflection point for AusperBio as we advance AHB-137 toward potential commercialization while developing next-generation therapies for CHB," said Dr. Guofeng Cheng, co-founder and CEO of AusperBio. "We are grateful for the continued confidence of our existing investors and pleased to welcome RA Capital to AusperBio. We look forward to building on this momentum to advance our strategy toward functional cure and unlock new opportunities across our oligonucleotide platforms." Dr. Chris Yang, co-founder and CSO of AusperBio, added, "AHB-137 has demonstrated promising clinical activity in patients and has the potential to serve as a backbone therapy for functional cure of CHB. Our Med-OligoTM ASO, Au-HALOTM targeted delivery and siRNA discovery platforms enable complementary approaches designed to achieve deeper and more durable antiviral responses. This financing will enable us to further advance these platforms and build on their potential to generate differentiated targeted oligonucleotide therapies for CHB and other diseases with significant unmet medical needs." Story continues About AHB-137 AHB-137 is AusperBio's lead investigational unconjugated antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB), developed using the Company's proprietary Med-OligoTM ASO platform. AHB-137 is designed to suppress hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) production, inhibit viral DNA replication, and promote immune reactivation, with the goal of achieving a functional cure for CHB. AHB-137 has demonstrated promising clinical results and is currently being evaluated in a Phase 3 trial in China, following completion of a global Phase 1 study and multiple Phase 2 studies. The Company is advancing AHB-137 through a coordinated global development strategy toward potential commercialization. AHB-137 is an investigational product candidate and has not been approved by any regulatory authority. About AHB-171 AHB-171 is an investigational hepatocyte-targeted siRNA therapeutic candidate for the treatment of CHB that leverages AusperBio's proprietary Au-HALOTM liver-targeting delivery platform. AHB-171 is designed to selectively suppress viral gene expression and provide potent and sustained antiviral activity. As the first clinical candidate developed using the Au-HALOTM platform, AHB-171 is advancing the clinical validation of the Company's targeted delivery and siRNA capabilities and broadening the Company's differentiated HBV pipeline. AHB-171 is an investigational product candidate and has not been approved by any regulatory authority. About Chronic Hepatitis B Chronic hepatitis B remains a significant global health burden, affecting an estimated 254 million people worldwide and causing approximately 1.1 million deaths annually, primarily from cirrhosis and liver cancer, according to the World Health Organization. Current therapies can suppress viral replication but rarely achieve a functional cure, leaving many patients requiring long-term treatment. About AusperBio AusperBio is a near-commercial biopharmaceutical company focused on developing differentiated oligonucleotide therapeutics and targeted delivery technologies, with an initial focus on achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B. The Company's innovation engine is built on its proprietary Med-OligoTM ASO and Au-HALOTM targeted delivery platforms, supporting the development of therapies across multiple oligonucleotide modalities. With multiple clinical-stage programs and a growing pipeline, AusperBio is advancing a backbone-based combination strategy for functional cure of CHB while exploring opportunities in additional disease areas with significant unmet medical needs. (2)广泛激活先天性和适应性免疫细胞; (3)普遍增强抗原呈递功能; (4)扰乱免疫调节检查点。 这些变化共同构成了PegIFNα诱导的全身性免疫激活状态,这正是其疗效与不良反应的基础。这种强大的免疫应答对清除感染肝细胞至关重要,也成为影响旁组织功能的主要因素。具体机制如下: PegIFNα诱导的全身性免疫激活:驱动抗病毒疗效与不良反应的免疫级联应答 分子信号通路(图A):PegIFNα结合IFNAR并激活JAK-STAT信号通路,从而诱导干扰素刺激基因(ISG)的转录。该信号级联应答会因细胞类型而异。 先天免疫扩增(图B):在巨噬细胞和树突状细胞中,JAK-STAT激活可诱导细胞因子释放,包括TNF-α、IL-6和IFN-γ。在受控条件下,这些局部细胞因子可增强抗原呈递,促进Th1极化,并招募NK细胞,从而发挥抗病毒作用。当细胞因子在全身过度扩增,可导致流感样症状等不良反应。 适应性免疫重塑(图C):在PegIFNα以及IL-12、IL-6、TNF-α和IFN-γ等细胞因子的驱动下,HBV特异性CD8+ T细胞通过颗粒酶B、穿孔素和IFN-γ清除受感染的肝细胞;Tfh细胞通过IL-21促进HBsAb的产生;Th1细胞增强抗病毒免疫应答;效应B细胞则产生HBsAb。另一方面,自身反应性T细胞和B细胞也可能通过抗-TPO和抗-Tg抗体导致组织损伤。 临床结局(图D):当免疫应答聚焦于受感染的肝细胞时,可实现临床治愈;而当免疫应答发生错误导向时,则可能出现多系统不良反应。 PegIFNα相关的不良反应并非偶发副作用,而是其主要机制——即PegIFNα诱导的全身性免疫激活——直接且可预测的结局。疗效所需的免疫激活与导致不良反应的免疫机理之间存在不可分割的联系。 三 PegIFNα治疗的不良反应管理策略 临床管理以主动监测和及时分级干预为基础。总体目标是维持一个可行的治疗窗口,平衡抗病毒疗效与安全性。在临床管理中需采取双向策略:第一,通过剖析个体易感性进行治疗前风险预测;第二,采用动态的、基于循证的干预措施进行治疗中管理,以维持可行的治疗窗口。需定期监测血常规、生化指标和甲状腺功能,监测频率应根据治疗阶段和患者稳定性进行调整。支持性护理对于缓解症状和提高治疗依从性至关重要。 参考文献: Zhu L, Peng F, Pi D, et al. Mechanisms and management of pegylated interferon-α toxicity in chronic hepatitis B[J]. Front Immunol, 2026, 17: 1801043. 阅读全文 你可能还想了解: PegIFNα治疗导致的流感样症状与普通流感在临床表现上有何区别? (2)广泛激活先天性和适应性免疫细胞; (3)普遍增强抗原呈递功能; (4)扰乱免疫调节检查点。 这些变化共同构成了PegIFNα诱导的全身性免疫激活状态,这正是其疗效与不良反应的基础。这种强大的免疫应答对清除感染肝细胞至关重要,也成为影响旁组织功能的主要因素。具体机制如下: PegIFNα诱导的全身性免疫激活:驱动抗病毒疗效与不良反应的免疫级联应答 分子信号通路(图A):PegIFNα结合IFNAR并激活JAK-STAT信号通路,从而诱导干扰素刺激基因(ISG)的转录。该信号级联应答会因细胞类型而异。 先天免疫扩增(图B):在巨噬细胞和树突状细胞中,JAK-STAT激活可诱导细胞因子释放,包括TNF-α、IL-6和IFN-γ。在受控条件下,这些局部细胞因子可增强抗原呈递,促进Th1极化,并招募NK细胞,从而发挥抗病毒作用。当细胞因子在全身过度扩增,可导致流感样症状等不良反应。 适应性免疫重塑(图C):在PegIFNα以及IL-12、IL-6、TNF-α和IFN-γ等细胞因子的驱动下,HBV特异性CD8+ T细胞通过颗粒酶B、穿孔素和IFN-γ清除受感染的肝细胞;Tfh细胞通过IL-21促进HBsAb的产生;Th1细胞增强抗病毒免疫应答;效应B细胞则产生HBsAb。另一方面,自身反应性T细胞和B细胞也可能通过抗-TPO和抗-Tg抗体导致组织损伤。 临床结局(图D):当免疫应答聚焦于受感染的肝细胞时,可实现临床治愈;而当免疫应答发生错误导向时,则可能出现多系统不良反应。 PegIFNα相关的不良反应并非偶发副作用,而是其主要机制——即PegIFNα诱导的全身性免疫激活——直接且可预测的结局。疗效所需的免疫激活与导致不良反应的免疫机理之间存在不可分割的联系。 三 PegIFNα治疗的不良反应管理策略 临床管理以主动监测和及时分级干预为基础。总体目标是维持一个可行的治疗窗口,平衡抗病毒疗效与安全性。在临床管理中需采取双向策略:第一,通过剖析个体易感性进行治疗前风险预测;第二,采用动态的、基于循证的干预措施进行治疗中管理,以维持可行的治疗窗口。需定期监测血常规、生化指标和甲状腺功能,监测频率应根据治疗阶段和患者稳定性进行调整。支持性护理对于缓解症状和提高治疗依从性至关重要。 参考文献: Zhu L, Peng F, Pi D, et al. Mechanisms and management of pegylated interferon-α toxicity in chronic hepatitis B[J]. Front Immunol, 2026, 17: 1801043. 阅读全文 你可能还想了解: PegIFNα治疗导致的流感样症状与普通流感在临床表现上有何区别? analysis.time: The article was published on 2026-08-26, with some event-related information dated to 2026-08-25. The evidence spans multiple studies and reports from 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The article discusses studies and clinical outcomes related to chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients in various locations, including Shanghai, and mentions general populations of patients with HBV infection.
analysis.event: The article provides an overview of the mechanisms and clinical outcomes of pegylated interferon alpha (PegIFNα) in the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB), including its role in immune activation and the management of adverse effects. It is a review article and not a confirmed outbreak or event.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: PegIFNα treatment has been associated with a clinical cure rate of approximately 30% in certain CHB patient groups. Adverse reactions include flu-like symptoms, injection site reactions, blood cell reduction, insomnia, thyroid dysfunction, and nausea. These are generally manageable and reversible, but may impact treatment adherence and safety.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The article presents a review of clinical studies and expert guidelines on the use of PegIFNα for CHB, including management strategies for adverse effects. It does not report any unresolved information or limitations in the source material.

analysis.brief_en: This article, published on August 26, 2026, by MedSci.cn, provides an in-depth review of the mechanisms and clinical outcomes of pegylated interferon alpha (PegIFNα) in the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB). PegIFNα is highlighted as a key drug for achieving clinical cure in CHB due to its ability to activate the host's immune system, reversing immune dysfunction and T-cell exhaustion. However, this immune activation can also lead to adverse effects such as flu-like symptoms, injection site reactions, blood cell reduction, insomnia, thyroid dysfunction, and nausea. These effects are generally manageable and reversible, but require careful monitoring and intervention. The article references several studies and expert guidelines from 2026, including the release of the 2026 'Pegylated Interferon-α Toxicity Management Expert Opinion,' which aims to assist clinicians in balancing the therapeutic benefits and safety of PegIFNα. The findings are based on clinical data and do not indicate any outbreak or public health emergency. The article is a review and does not report any confirmed or suspected cases of viral transmission or infection events.

news.title_zh: 【期刊导读】通往临床治愈路上的“信号灯”:读懂聚乙二醇干扰素α的免疫激活信号-MedSci.cn - 梅斯医学 MedSci
news.source_body_en: This article, published on August 26, 2026, by MedSci.cn, provides an in-depth review of the mechanisms and clinical outcomes of pegylated interferon alpha (PegIFNα) in the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB). PegIFNα is highlighted as a key drug for achieving clinical cure in CHB due to its ability to activate the host's immune system, reversing immune dysfunction and T-cell exhaustion. However, this immune activation can also lead to adverse effects such as flu-like symptoms, injection site reactions, blood cell reduction, insomnia, thyroid dysfunction, and nausea. These effects are generally manageable and reversible, but require careful monitoring and intervention. The article references several studies and expert guidelines from 2026, including the release of the 2026 'Pegylated Interferon-α Toxicity Management Expert Opinion,' which aims to assist clinicians in balancing the therapeutic benefits and safety of PegIFNα. The findings are based on clinical data and do not indicate any outbreak or public health emergency. The article is a review and does not report any confirmed or suspected cases of viral transmission or infection events.
news.content_zh: 该文章于2026年8月26日发表于MedSci.cn,对慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)的治疗中聚乙二醇化干扰素α(PegIFNα)的作用机制和临床结果进行了深入综述。PegIFNα 因其能够激活 宿主 的免疫系统、逆转免疫功能障碍和 T 细胞耗竭而被强调为实现 CHB 临床治愈的关键药物。然而,这种免疫激活也会导致不良反应,例如流感样症状、注射部位反应、血细胞减少、失眠、甲状腺功能障碍和恶心。这些影响通常是可控和可逆的,但需要仔细监测和干预。文章引用了 2026 年的多项研究和专家指南,包括发布的 2026 年《聚乙二醇化干扰素-α 毒性管理专家意见》,旨在帮助临床医生平衡 PegIFNα 的治疗益处和安全性。该研究结果基于临床数据,并不表明任何 暴发 或公共卫生紧急情况。文章为综述,不报道任何确诊或疑似病毒传播病例或感染事件。

Sign in/Sign up Subscribe Support local news Sign out Opinion Gift Gift this article Copy Link Email Facebook X Bluesky Threads WhatsApp Gift this article Copy Link Email Facebook X Bluesky Threads WhatsApp Share Share this article Copy Link Email Facebook X Bluesky Threads WhatsApp Share this article Copy Link Email Facebook X Bluesky Threads WhatsApp Why we need vaccines As Pennsylvania grapples with two deaths from measles, the former health commissioner of Philadelphia offers a novel way to think about vaccinations — as providing soldiers for a war against enemies. Add The InquirerUs on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in your search results. There is a lot of misunderstanding surrounding vaccines, but their greatest value is in creating the antibodies to fight off initial infections, writes Walter Tsou.Read moreLM Otero / AP by Walter Tsou, For The Inquirer Published Aug. 27, 2026, 10:01 a.m. ET Listen to article • 0:00 min Imagine you are a general about to go to war. The enemies are known to be fierce fighters. Would you rather have three soldiers on your side or 300,000? Let’s personalize it. You are the general of your body under attack by a new flesh-eating bacterium. Would you rather have three antibodies on your side or 300,000 antibodies? Survival or death? Pretty easy choice. There is a lot of misunderstanding surrounding vaccines, but their greatest value is in creating the antibodies to fight off initial infections. President Donald Trump, now playing a role as pseudo-physician, has announced an executive order to reduce the number of childhood vaccines from 17 to 11. Hepatitis B, one of the nastiest viruses, is among the vaccines that are no longer required. Hepatitis B is a highly infectious virus, even more infectious than HIV. Undetected, it can pass from a mother who is carrying the virus to a baby during birth, infecting the newborn on Day One of life. Months later, the virus has infected the liver, causing the newborn to be fatigued, not eating, maybe even jaundiced. Years later, they can develop chronic hepatitis B and even liver failure or cancer. What is remarkable is that all of this is preventable with a vaccine administered at birth. Americans are very concerned about healthcare costs. The greatest way to cut healthcare costs is to prevent the disease in the first place. The more antibodies in our bodies able to fight the onslaught of viruses out in this hostile world, the more likely we will be in preventing disease in the first place. People, including Trump, wonder why there are so many vaccines. There are three factors: First is that there are a lot of bacterial and viral diseases. Each needs its own unique antibodies to fight them. There are a lot more than just 11 or even 17 viruses or bacteria in the world — which is why new recommendations and combinations are tested and recommended. Second is that researchers can measure antibody levels, and building up enough antibodies to defeat diseases may require more than one shot. At least two current vaccines can prevent cancer. Finally, viruses are very tricky and can mutate, camouflaging their detection from existing antibodies. Classic viruses that have this capability are influenza and SARS-CoV-2 (the virus that causes COVID-19). So recommendations have changed to reflect the changing flu and COVID shots to be given annually rather than just once and done. Vaccine researchers are on the cusp of even greater breakthroughs. At least two current vaccines can prevent cancer. The HPV vaccine prevents human papillomavirus from infecting the cervix, which, in turn, prevents cervical cancer. HPV has also been linked to head and neck cancer. And the aforementioned hepatitis B vaccine can help prevent liver cancer. The Nobel Prize-winning discovery of mRNA vaccines developed by Philadelphia scientists is being used to create inactive tumor proteins that our immune system can recognize. Future researchers will be able to identify our personal cancers, create individual tumor proteins that our immune systems will recognize, and create a personalized immune response that can kill cancers in our bodies. These are heady times in medical research, which desperately needs the support of our government. Unfortunately, many of these discoveries, including new vaccines against scourges like Ebola, bird flu, hantavirus, malaria, and many others, are being stopped by our failure to invest in research. It is a lost opportunity to prevent disease using our own bodies’ immune system by creating an army of antibodies at the ready. And nothing is more frightening than trying to fight a virus with only three antibodies. Walter Tsou is the former health commissioner of Philadelphia and the past president of the Philadelphia County Medical Society. WT Walter Tsou, For The Inquirer Sign in/Sign up Subscribe Support local news Sign out Opinion Gift Gift this article Copy Link Email Facebook X Bluesky Threads WhatsApp Gift this article Copy Link Email Facebook X Bluesky Threads WhatsApp Share Share this article Copy Link Email Facebook X Bluesky Threads WhatsApp Share this article Copy Link Email Facebook X Bluesky Threads WhatsApp Why we need vaccines As Pennsylvania grapples with two deaths from measles, the former health commissioner of Philadelphia offers a novel way to think about vaccinations — as providing soldiers for a war against enemies. Add The InquirerUs on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in your search results. There is a lot of misunderstanding surrounding vaccines, but their greatest value is in creating the antibodies to fight off initial infections, writes Walter Tsou.Read moreLM Otero / AP by Walter Tsou, For The Inquirer Published Aug. 27, 2026, 10:01 a.m. ET Listen to article • 0:00 min Imagine you are a general about to go to war. The enemies are known to be fierce fighters. Would you rather have three soldiers on your side or 300,000? Let’s personalize it. You are the general of your body under attack by a new flesh-eating bacterium. Would you rather have three antibodies on your side or 300,000 antibodies? Survival or death? Pretty easy choice. There is a lot of misunderstanding surrounding vaccines, but their greatest value is in creating the antibodies to fight off initial infections. President Donald Trump, now playing a role as pseudo-physician, has announced an executive order to reduce the number of childhood vaccines from 17 to 11. Hepatitis B, one of the nastiest viruses, is among the vaccines that are no longer required. Hepatitis B is a highly infectious virus, even more infectious than HIV. Undetected, it can pass from a mother who is carrying the virus to a baby during birth, infecting the newborn on Day One of life. Months later, the virus has infected the liver, causing the newborn to be fatigued, not eating, maybe even jaundiced. Years later, they can develop chronic hepatitis B and even liver failure or cancer. What is remarkable is that all of this is preventable with a vaccine administered at birth. Americans are very concerned about healthcare costs. The greatest way to cut healthcare costs is to prevent the disease in the first place. The more antibodies in our bodies able to fight the onslaught of viruses out in this hostile world, the more likely we will be in preventing disease in the first place. People, including Trump, wonder why there are so many vaccines. There are three factors: First is that there are a lot of bacterial and viral diseases. Each needs its own unique antibodies to fight them. There are a lot more than just 11 or even 17 viruses or bacteria in the world — which is why new recommendations and combinations are tested and recommended. Second is that researchers can measure antibody levels, and building up enough antibodies to defeat diseases may require more than one shot. At least two current vaccines can prevent cancer. Finally, viruses are very tricky and can mutate, camouflaging their detection from existing antibodies. Classic viruses that have this capability are influenza and SARS-CoV-2 (the virus that causes COVID-19). So recommendations have changed to reflect the changing flu and COVID shots to be given annually rather than just once and done. Vaccine researchers are on the cusp of even greater breakthroughs. At least two current vaccines can prevent cancer. The HPV vaccine prevents human papillomavirus from infecting the cervix, which, in turn, prevents cervical cancer. HPV has also been linked to head and neck cancer. And the aforementioned hepatitis B vaccine can help prevent liver cancer. The Nobel Prize-winning discovery of mRNA vaccines developed by Philadelphia scientists is being used to create inactive tumor proteins that our immune system can recognize. Future researchers will be able to identify our personal cancers, create individual tumor proteins that our immune systems will recognize, and create a personalized immune response that can kill cancers in our bodies. These are heady times in medical research, which desperately needs the support of our government. Unfortunately, many of these discoveries, including new vaccines against scourges like Ebola, bird flu, hantavirus, malaria, and many others, are being stopped by our failure to invest in research. It is a lost opportunity to prevent disease using our own bodies’ immune system by creating an army of antibodies at the ready. And nothing is more frightening than trying to fight a virus with only three antibodies. Walter Tsou is the former health commissioner of Philadelphia and the past president of the Philadelphia County Medical Society. WT Walter Tsou, For The Inquirer analysis.brief_en: The article published on August 27, 2026, by Walter Tsou, former health commissioner of Philadelphia, discusses the importance of vaccines in building immunity against diseases like hepatitis B. It highlights that hepatitis B is highly infectious and can lead to severe outcomes such as chronic infection, liver failure, and cancer, which are preventable with a vaccine given at birth. The piece also references President Donald Trump's executive order to reduce the number of childhood vaccines from 17 to 11, noting that hepatitis B is among the vaccines being removed. Tsou argues that vaccines are essential for creating antibodies to fight infections and that the government must support medical research to develop new vaccines and personalized immune responses. The article emphasizes the risks of relying on only a few antibodies to combat viruses and calls for increased investment in vaccine development to prevent diseases and their associated healthcare costs.

news.title_zh: 为什么我们需要 疫苗 - Inquirer.com
news.source_body_en: The article published on August 27, 2026, by Walter Tsou, former health commissioner of Philadelphia, discusses the importance of vaccines in building immunity against diseases like hepatitis B. It highlights that hepatitis B is highly infectious and can lead to severe outcomes such as chronic infection, liver failure, and cancer, which are preventable with a vaccine given at birth. The piece also references President Donald Trump's executive order to reduce the number of childhood vaccines from 17 to 11, noting that hepatitis B is among the vaccines being removed. Tsou argues that vaccines are essential for creating antibodies to fight infections and that the government must support medical research to develop new vaccines and personalized immune responses. The article emphasizes the risks of relying on only a few antibodies to combat viruses and calls for increased investment in vaccine development to prevent diseases and their associated healthcare costs.
news.content_zh: 费城前卫生专员 Walter Tsou 于 2026 年 8 月 27 日发表的文章讨论了 疫苗 在增强乙型肝炎等疾病免疫力方面的重要性。文章强调,乙型肝炎具有高度传染性,可导致慢性感染、肝衰竭和癌症等严重后果,而这些疾病在出生时服用 疫苗 是可以预防的。这篇文章还提到了唐纳德·特朗普总统的行政命令,将儿童 疫苗 的数量从 17 人减少到 11 人,并指出乙型肝炎是被删除的 疫苗 之一。Tsou 认为,疫苗 对于制造抗感染抗体至关重要,政府必须支持医学研究来开发新的 疫苗 和个性化 免疫应答。该文章强调了仅依靠少数抗体来对抗病毒的风险,并呼吁增加对 疫苗 开发的投资,以预防疾病及其相关的医疗费用。

analysis.brief_en: On August 25, 2026, MT Newswires reported that GSK's investigational therapy Hibsago has been granted approval by Japanese health authorities, marking the first instance of a drug being designated a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B. The approval targets individuals living with chronic HBV infection in Japan and signals a potential shift in treatment paradigms, aiming for sustained viral suppression without lifelong therapy. The announcement did not include data on patient numbers, clinical outcomes, or safety profiles, and no additional information on post‐approval monitoring or distribution plans was provided. As a result, while the regulatory decision represents a significant milestone, the broader public‐health impact and any associated risks remain to be clarified.

news.content_zh: 2026 年 8 月 25 日,MT Newswires 报道称,葛兰素史克的研究疗法 Hibsago 已获得日本卫生当局的批准,这标志着该药物首次被指定为 慢性乙型肝炎 的 功能性治愈。此次批准针对的是日本慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染者,标志着 治疗 范式的潜在转变,旨在实现持续病毒抑制,无需终身治疗。该公告不包括患者数量、临床结果或安全概况的数据,也没有提供有关批准后监测或分配计划的其他信息。因此,虽然监管决定代表了一个重要的里程碑,但更广泛的公共卫生影响和任何相关风险仍有待澄清。

supplementary_news.content: Therapy Area Allergy & Immunology Cardiology Dermatology Diabetes Flagship Journal Gastroenterology General Healthcare Hematology Hepatology Innovations Interventional Cardiology Microbiology & Infectious Diseases Nephrology Neurology Oncology Radiology Reproductive Health Respiratory Rheumatology Urology Podcasts Journals Webinars Congress Hub Toolkit Paediatric Growth Calculator DVT Risk Calculator Due Date Calculator Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP) Calculator BMI Calculator Collaborate About EQOH Careers Contact Us Media Pack Editorial Enquiries Contributors & Authors Submit a Paper Media Partners Work With Us EMJ Interactive EMJ GOLD CME search Join FREE This site is intended for healthcare professionals You must accept all conditions before being able to view the post Continue EUR USA EUR USA Therapy Area Allergy & Immunology Cardiology Dermatology Diabetes Flagship Journal Gastroenterology General Healthcare Hematology Hepatology Innovations Interventional Cardiology Microbiology & Infectious Diseases Nephrology Neurology Oncology Radiology Reproductive Health Respiratory Rheumatology Urology Podcasts Journals Webinars Congress Hub Toolkit Paediatric Growth Calculator DVT Risk Calculator Due Date Calculator Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP) Calculator BMI Calculator Collaborate About EQOH Careers Contact Us Media Pack Editorial Enquiries Contributors & Authors Submit a Paper Media Partners Work With Us EMJ Interactive EMJ GOLD CME Join FREE Search type Keyword Author Home EMJ GOLD GSK wins approval for new hepatitis B drug GSK wins approval for new hepatitis B drug 24 Aug 2026 EMJ GOLD View All News Key Summary: Bepirovirsen has been approved in Japan as a functional cure treatment for chronic hepatitis B. GSK predicts the hepatitis B drug could generate over £2bn in peak annual sales. The FDA will prioritise its review of Jemperli as a potential treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer. GSK has received its first global approval for its chronic hepatitis B drug and key support for a potential rectal cancer therapy, it announced on Monday. The British pharmaceutical giant shared that bepirovirsen, to be branded as Hibsago, has been approved as the first and only functional cure for chronic hepatitis B in Japan – where it is estimated over 800,000 people live with the disease, according to the WHO. First functional cure for hepatitis B The approval comes after successful late-stage trials proved the drug to be successful in helping one in five patients reach a functional cure for hepatitis B. Bepirovirsen works by blocking viral DNA replication, lowering hepatitis B surface antigen levels in the blood and boosting the immune response for longer lasting control of the virus, tackling the disease three-fold. As the first approved finite treatment course that can be used as an alternative to lifelong antiviral pills to achieve functional cure, it leads the way for a new wave of next-generation therapies. GSK has predicted that the new drug could bring in over £2bn ($2.73bn) in peak annual sales, bringing it closer to its annual revenue goal of over £40bn by 2031. Cancer therapy review expected The firm also announced that the FDA has committed to carrying out a priority review of another of its drugs, Jemperli (dostarlimab), as a potential treatment for a type of rectal cancer, alongside its existing approvals for specific endometrial cancer subtypes. The FDA has assigned February 2027 as the action date for the rectal cancer review, with the program structure possibly yielding a decision earlier. Jemperli, which is not currently approved anywhere in the world for the treatment of locally advanced rectal cancer, also received Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track designations by the FDA. These two regulatory wins for the company come just weeks after it launched a £1.9bn ($2.52bn) cost-savings effort to help fund its expanded late-stage study roster and deliver on CEO Luke Miels’ promise for faster drug development. The restructuring is a major step by the company’s boss to reassure investors that GSK can navigate a looming patent deadline for its blockbuster HIV drug, dolutegravir, between 2028 and 2030. HIV is currently the company’s leading specialty therapy area by revenue, but GSK said it now expects to start 25 late-stage studies by the end of 2026 in an effort to continue to expand pipelines in oncology and respiratory, immunology and inflammation.
